| [CLAIM-148](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-148.md) v4 | A matrix factorization is identified only up to an invertible change of latent coordinates, which weight decay narrows to rotations and nonnegativity to rescalings and permutations plus a data-dependent remainder; such a gauge is not a symmetry of the relational system, and automorphisms of the data act on the factors only when the factorization is identifiable | Drawn by the assistant at A207 §3, made explicit at A214 §6 and kept in A218 (§4.2, Ch5.4–5.9). It does not say latent axes are meaningless, or that observed data have non-trivial automorphisms. | Active |

It carries [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md)'s remedy from correspondences to training objectives. Kynkäänniemi et al. ([CASE-041](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-041.md)) is a documented instance, which the exchange did not know of. The documented support is one training case, in image generation, and one selection case, in translation (CASE-071). | Active |
| [CLAIM-150](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md) v2 | An ontology of intrinsically individuated objects with relational properties can reproduce the categorical and operational identifications, and the predictions, of a relational one, so identification underdetermines constitution | The exchange's own guard, stated six times (A187, A191 §4, A198 §VI, A203 §35, A214 §13, A218 §13). | [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) v6 | Any individuation built on sufficiency is relative to the target it is sufficient for: fix the outcomes differently and a different partition wins, so no boundary drawn this way is universal | Dual-filed from [MOM-POS-001](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/positions.d/POS-001.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). A sufficient statistic is sufficient for a target Y, so every partition chosen as minimal sufficient inherits Y. MOM's example: fix the outcomes differently and "organism" wins instead of "animal". In this record it is the standing caution on every boundary criterion filed beside it ([CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), [CLAIM-161](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md)). It does not say boundaries are arbitrary, only that each is relative to a stated target. | Active |
| [CLAIM-153](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md) | Failure of a self to hold together across contexts is a monodromy around a cycle of contexts: any two locally consistent contexts glue, and the minimal model of the obstruction needs three | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-165](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-165.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). Model contexts (roles, personas, sub-agents) as a cover, and the offsets that reconcile neighbours as a cochain. A global section, one coherent self, exists exactly when the monodromy Φ around a cycle vanishes. Two contexts always glue, so compartmentalization needs a loop. The frustrated XY or Kuramoto energy finds the obstruction: its minimum is 0 exactly when Φ ≡ 0. Abelian case only; re-checked here. | Active |
| [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) v3 | A candidate structure is worth naming as a unit when its effect-to-noise ratio outruns the Occam cost of keeping it: reify when d'² exceeds the log prior-to-posterior variance ratio, where the model with the candidate stays regular at the parameters that switch it off | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-160](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-160.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). By the Savage–Dickey ratio, ln BF(keep) = ½(d'² − Occam), so a direction, block or sector is real enough to name exactly when δ/ε > τ with τ² = ln(s²/σ²), the information the data added about it. In this record it prices the boundary tests for a combined form: a near-decomposable block ([LIT-905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md)) earns a name when its gap beats its Occam factor. Re-checked here in the conjugate case. Narrowed to candidates whose model stays regular where they are switched off; where it is singular the rule overcharges (CLAIM-188). | Active |
| [CLAIM-159](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-159.md) v3 | The record's rival accounts of will are claims about drive profiles in different cells: Ainslie's interests are aggregate or emergent, the expected value of control is top-down, and will-organization is the maintained organization that governs how the drive profile changes | The assistant's reading, offered in chat on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's prompt. Ainslie's will has no governor: the person is "just the resultant" of bargaining interests, which is aggregate, or emergent if resolve is a property only the recursion has. The expected value of control posits a dedicated specifying system, which is top-down. The will paper's will-organization is the maintained organization of relations that decides which regime is effective, so it governs the drive profile's changes over time. That is the owner's point that "who drives" is not constant. | Active |
| [CLAIM-164](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-164.md) v4 | What a spectral gap makes definite is the subspace of the cluster it isolates, not a single direction: the gap picks the object, and the object is a vector only when its own gap is wide | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-144](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-144.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). Under a perturbation δT, the subspace spanned by a cluster of singular values separated by a gap δ rotates by at most ‖δT‖/δ (Davis–Kahan), whatever happens to the vectors inside it. So the well-defined unit is the gap-isolated projector. Re-measured here. With [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) it is a criterion: the gap picks the object, and the Occam factor says whether the gap is big enough. | Active |
| [CLAIM-175](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md) v3 | A partner-dancing couple, while dancing, is one combined cognitive form on the extended-mind thesis's own terms, more clearly than Otto and his notebook, and merits a name of its own | The owner's reply of 2026-10-11 to the dancers objection, which they had not read: "under extended mind thesis, I'd argue that the pair, while dancing together, comprises a combined form that merits some privileged nomenclature of some kind". Clark & Chalmers endorse socially extended cognition, and the objection's own source calls the interaction an autonomous process. So the objection fails against the combined form and survives only as a question about selfhood. The name is not yet chosen. | Active |
| [CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) v2 | In the record's exchanges with collaborators who keep no memory, the argument repeatedly loses identity: concepts are redefined silently, objections and readings come back as though new, and the thesis changes without anyone arguing for the change | Stated as a finding in [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md), from seven readers coding the will exchange, and found again in the What Survives Translation? exchange by the workbench reconstructions of 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10. Filed on 2026-10-11 as the first premise of the manuscript. Two exchanges with one owner and one assistant family, so Proposed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-188](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-188.md) v4 | Where the model with a candidate structure is singular at the parameters that switch the candidate off, with real log canonical threshold λ below d/2 and multiplicity m, the reification rule's Gaussian Occam term overcharges keeping the candidate by (d/2 − λ) log n + (m − 1) log log n to leading order, so near the threshold the rule prunes candidates the Bayes factor keeps, and its derivation holds only where that model stays regular | A narrowing of [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), filed on 2026-10-11 from a synthesis review that found the record already held the readings that limit it. [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)'s rule prices a candidate with a Gaussian Occam factor, which is exact in the conjugate case it was re-checked in. The candidates it is meant for (blocks, sectors, couplings with hidden structure) are often singular where they are switched off. There THEORY-087 puts the penalty at λ log n − (m − 1) log log n, not (d/2) log n. On CASE-152's product model the rule prunes, near the threshold, candidates the exact Bayes factor keeps. CLAIM-154 is narrowed to models that stay regular at the switch-off. | Active |
| [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md) v4 | A gap or coupling criterion cannot tell a boundary a system produces from one imposed on it: a membrane the cell makes and a beam joining two pendulums pass alike, so the block test cannot by itself supply the individuality minimal agency needs | A counter to the block criterion and to the agency test's first condition, found by two separate reviews of the unlinked THEORYs in the third synthesis pass. It grants the target-relativity [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) states. Its point is different: with the target fixed, a near-decomposability gap is a statistic of coupling, and coupling is the same whether the system made the boundary or something else did. [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) and THEORY-1119 place the line at production and self-distinction instead. No case has been measured: the point is that a coupling statistic has no term for who made the coupling. | Active |
| [CLAIM-195](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-195.md) v2 | For an argument, the constraint set that persistence is relative to is fixed by an amendable decision, not discovered: the record stipulates what counts as the same claim persisting, which makes the choice explicit without making it non-arbitrary | Files the point the workbench of 2026-10-11 (214308) left as notes on [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) and [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md). Viability is relative to a constraint set the theory does not supply ([THEORY-134](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md)), and the will-organization line leaves "who fixes the constraint set" open ([CLAIM-079](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-079.md), [ARG-007](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-007.md)). For an argument the record fixes it by decision ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) and its successors), so the set is explicit and amendable. That shows how one system fixes its set; it does not show the choice is non-arbitrary. | Active |
| [CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) | Sections over contexts that do not overlap always glue, so a sense that differs between disjoint contexts is not a gluing failure: a failure needs an overlap carrying sections that disagree, and which families count as covers decides whether anything glues | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-088](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-088.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). The sheaf condition says a family of sections that agree on overlaps glues to one global section. Where two contexts do not overlap, agreement is vacuous and they glue. So "tall", which takes one threshold for people and another for trees, is one global section with the comparison class part of the meaning, not a failure of gluing. A failure needs contexts that overlap and carry sections that disagree there. Which families count as covering is the piece that decides whether anything glues, and a sheaf picture of meaning that does not state it has decided nothing. | Active |
| [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md) v3 | Blackwell's order bounds what a rendering makes possible for any receiver, and a given receiver's access is usable information relative to the rules it can apply, which a garbling can raise for that receiver but never above what the source makes possible | The record's reconciliation, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-225](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md). Both standards are kept, in different roles: Blackwell's order is the ceiling, and [TERM-034](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-034.md)'s interpreter-relative fidelity ("relative to an interpreter and its available side information") is the receiver's. [CLAIM-087](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md)'s improvement is a gain in usable information. The nearest held reading is [THEORY-176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md)'s "Its loss bounds r's best attainable risk for that problem from above", for restricted rules. The example is checkable; whether real receivers show such gains is a proposal. The usable-information literature was not held when it was filed; Xu et al.'s V-information is now read (note of 2026-10-21). It does not say which rule class real readers have. | Active |
| [CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md) | The transports of Propositions 1–2 and of D_obs act on judgement outcomes, not texts, and for any one source–target pair a constant kernel transports any overlap-consistent target, so they constrain a translation only once one kernel family is fixed across many utterances and derived from the text channel | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The manuscript's kernels K_C map readers' judgements to readers' judgements, while a translation is a channel on texts, T(v \| u), and [TERM-008](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-008.md) records that the two levels are never formally related. For one source and any overlap-consistent target, the constant kernel makes D_obs zero and satisfies naturality. Granted, because it is elementary. It does not say [CLAIM-121](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-121.md) or [CLAIM-070](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-070.md) is false; it bears on what they are used to support. | Active |
| [CLAIM-208](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-208.md) v2 | The compositional predictions are upper bounds whose constants cannot be estimated from serial-reproduction data in a metric fixed beforehand, so the compositional half of the success criterion cannot fail | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The recursion e_n ≤ (∏κ_j)e_0 + Σε_i∏κ_j is a theorem once its constants are the true ones, so a chain cannot depart from it; it can only show a constant was misestimated. A sensitivity κ_i belongs to a reteller's kernel and needs many retellings of each of several inputs at every generation, where a chain gives one. And [CLAIM-059](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-059.md) says amplification "needs a metric other than total variation" (now held as CLAIM-267), so the regime depends on a metric chosen afterwards. [CLAIM-078](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-078.md) records that the compositional half was dropped from the manuscript, not that it cannot fail as stated. It does not say error propagation is unimportant. | Active |
| [CLAIM-210](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md) v2 | Sharing a kind and being a rendering are different relations: kind-sharing is symmetric and says what is to be preserved, while fidelity belongs to a transport from a given source, so an utterance of the same kind made independently of the source shares its kind and has no fidelity to it | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-246](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md). The October thesis puts fidelity in what persists "through those transformations", and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) makes fidelity the distortion profile of a transport. So the objection's independent utterance I shares the source's kind and has no fidelity to it, since no transport relates them; the translation T has both. T's provenance is a fact the transport clause supplies, not something the kind criterion must recover. [CLAIM-002](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s continuity of transmission concerns the identity of a work, which [TERM-040](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-040.md) keeps apart from the kind. Active, because it is read off the record's own texts. It does not say judges track descent. | Active |
