On those cases [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) and [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s fidelity clause give opposite verdicts on what survived, yet the two are joined by `complements`, which says they answer different parts of one question and do not compete, and [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) answers only [QUESTION-029](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-029.md). Granted: it is a comparison of texts and of the record's relations. It does not say which criterion is right. | Active |
| [CLAIM-214](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-214.md) | The distribution-over-situations criterion compares each language's own listener posterior, so it needs no correspondence of alternative sets; that a literal rendering can fail it is the criterion detecting a lost implicature, and a target language may admit no rendering that passes | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-236](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-236.md). [CLAIM-111](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md)'s criterion is P_o(z \| c_o, u_o) ≈ P_t(τ_z(z) \| c_t, u_t). On the rational-speech-act model each posterior is computed with its own language's alternatives, so comparing the posteriors needs no map between the alternative sets. The objection's worked case is right, and it shows the criterion rejecting a rendering that keeps the literal content and loses a scalar implicature. Active, because it is read off the criterion's form and checked by arithmetic. It does not say the model is right or that the criterion applies to poems. | Active |
| [CLAIM-216](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-216.md) v2 | A thesis that conjoins relational constitution, statistical recovery, transport and receivers' recovery is defeated whole by any one of its empirical findings, though its clauses can hold or fail apart, so the line is better put as separate theses, each with its own defeat condition, resting on one another only where one is a premise of another | The interlocutor's objection at U62 (A240) to the October thesis ([CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)) and to the record's restatement of it ([CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md)), given as the reason for superseding [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md): "Separates ontology, statistical recovery, and empirical transport instead of making them rise or fall together". The record's replies of 2026-10-10 had already separated the receiver thesis and the incremental thesis; the restatement joined the four clauses again under one defeat condition. Active since 2026-10-30; CLAIM-204 concedes it. It says what would answer it, and does not say an integrative statement is useless. | Active |
| [CLAIM-218](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-218.md) | The task-paired risk difference the record uses in place of Blackwell's order, D_Q = sup_q \|R_q(U) − R_τ(q)(V)\|, is a different quantity: it reduces each risk set to one number, needs the losses of paired tasks on one scale, and its absolute value counts improvement as distortion | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) is stated in Blackwell's order, and the record's decision term is A86's D_Q. A risk per task needs a prior or a minimax summary, where Blackwell's order compares whole risk sets. Subtracting the risks of two tasks needs their losses on one scale, which nothing supplies. The absolute value makes D_Q symmetric, against [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md). Granted, because each point is elementary. It objects to [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md) by undermining the measure meant to realize it, not [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s truth, and it does not say a decision term is unworkable. | Active |
| [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md) v4 | A change in the global compatibility of a fixed scenario is either a change in contextuality proper, which the behavioural data read show none of, or a change in overlap consistency, which is ordinary context dependence and moves by at most 2ε when each context moves by ε | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Dzhafarov, Zhang and Kujala ([LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md)) find no contextuality in five kinds of behavioural data, and [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md) reports that 34 of 90 language systems signal too much to be contextual. If pragmatic data are noncontextual as a rule, [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)'s defeat condition is met by default; what is left to change is overlap consistency, which is the "trivial sense of contextuality" and is fixed by the local distributions. The only instance of the headline is the stipulated [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md). Among the claims [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) is cited only by [CLAIM-041](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-041.md), not by [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md). The objection is open; it does not say a contextual pragmatic data set cannot exist. | Active |
| [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md) v2 | No design in the programme includes an interlingual translation, and the defeat conditions are disjunctive, so English retellings and model chains could settle a thesis about what survives translation | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens). The workbench entry for 2026-10-10 notes that the title's question "is left with no translated text in the programme"; no CLAIM says it, and none draws the consequence. Every stimulus set the designs name is English, or names no language; Villon→Henley and Marot→Hofstadter never enter a design. [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s defeat condition ranges over "translations, retellings or cross-modal renderings", so a result on English paraphrase alone can meet it. It does not say intralingual results are irrelevant. | Active |
| [CLAIM-223](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md) v2 | Whether a distinction survived is fixed by what the receivers can recover, and whether it can be shown to have survived is fixed by what the analyst's probes can identify, so the manuscript's thesis and the October fidelity clause, read so, answer different parts of one question | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-211](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md), and the argument [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) asked for: "the thesis now needs both conditions, or an argument for dropping one". It keeps both, in different roles. On [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md)'s cases: a distinction identifiable but unusable did not survive for those receivers; one usable but unidentifiable survived without evidence of it. Read so, `complements` is right on content. A proposal: it is a reading of [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md), not what A218 says. | Active |
| [CLAIM-225](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md) v4 | Blackwell's order measures what an ideal decision-maker could do, not what a given receiver can reconstruct, and the line's claims that a rendering can improve access describe garblings that real receivers do better with, which is the shape of the Blackwell thesis's own defeat condition | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange connects the two claims. A generator that sees only the text makes its image a garbling of the text about the situation, so by Blackwell's theorem the image is no better for any decision. [CLAIM-087](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md) says such an image can improve access. Either that effect is impossible, or judged access is not Blackwell informativeness, and then [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s standard is not the one [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s receiver and its defeat condition use. It meets the shape of [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s defeat condition, not its letter. It is distinct from [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md), which sets the analyst against the receiver: this sets the ideal receiver against an actual one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md) v2 | The defeat tests pool unnamed judges and treat their disagreement as noise, though the theory makes the act partly constituted by its audience; for historical sources there is no source audience at all, and for interlingual ones population differences are read as distortion | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A theory on which the act depends on its audience predicts structured variation between judges, so averaging a convenience sample measures an unnamed population's act. The source term of D(τ) for Villon, Henley or Marot can only be a modern reading, and for a live interlingual case the source and target judges are different communities, so the distance confounds population with transport. [CLAIM-074](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-074.md) says fidelity differs across interpreters, as a thesis; it is not applied to the tests. It does not say cross-population fidelity is meaningless. | Active |
| [CLAIM-227](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-227.md) | No validated measure of footing or stance exists in the record, and the one repeated assignment of footing, the analyst's own, changed between passes | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Footing and stance are the observables the central theses turn on, yet the only footing judgement made twice of the same texts, the assistant's labelling of its own four refrains, changed between A38 and A39 without comment ([CASE-012](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-012.md)), and no design gives judges a definition, a response format, a reliability target or a validation against a known contrast. Granted, because it is a reading of the record. It does not say footing cannot be measured. | Active |
| [CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) v3 | Blackwell comparison needs the state each rendering is about, which natural texts do not supply, so a decision measure is fixed by whoever labels the state, and it orders translation procedures, not single renderings | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Testing Blackwell's order needs the joint law of the situation and the signal. For natural texts the situation is what interpretation recovers, so it comes from the stimulus design, the analyst's labels or the judges, and decision-relevant information is measured against whoever fixed it. An experiment is a family of distributions, one per state, so a single rendering of a single poem is not one. [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s defeat condition, "one rendering is a garbling of another", is then not well typed. It does not say a design-based state is illegitimate. | Active |
| [CLAIM-231](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-231.md) | On observed responses, a rendering that keeps the response distribution of each order of two framings within ε of the source's, under an outcome correspondence, keeps the observed order effect within 2ε, a bound identified from data, while the intertwining identity bounds it only through defects of an unidentified state model | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, after [CLAIM-253](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md). The commutator identity of the manuscript's §9 holds, and its defects are not identified from data, by the objection's hidden-bit construction. What can be estimated is the response distribution under each order, so the bound is restated on those: a special case of observational distortion with contexts indexed by framing order. Active, because it is elementary and checkable. It does not say the state-model account is wrong, and it does not identify the defects. | Active |
| [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md) v3 | Human ratings of stance or footing and human ratings of fidelity of the same renderings share rater construal, scale use and a general impression, which a machine similarity score shares with neither | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Ratings of stance and footing share rater construal, scale use and the reading of one stimulus with ratings of fidelity, and an embedding score shares none of that. The manuscript's split annotators (§10, as [QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) reports) remove the shared rater, not the shared construal. It is a second reason, beside [CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), that the central tests are easy to pass. Open, because a design could answer it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md) v2 | The central theses' defeat conditions pit them only against embedding, propositional or surface similarity, and every rival account the record names (functional equivalence, Gutt's interpretive resemblance, speech-act pragmatics) also predicts that judged pragmatic observables beat text similarity | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure and empirical lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. Every thesis-level defeat condition in the line has one form: human judgements of fidelity or of shared kind are predicted as well by a text-similarity score as by the theory's measures. [CLAIM-023](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-023.md) says the pragmatic point is not new, and a functional-equivalence, relevance-theoretic or speech-act account passes the same test. Granted, because it is read off the texts. It does not say the theses are false, only that their stated tests cannot separate them from the positions they claim to improve on. | Active |
| [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md) v3 | The line's proposed quantities have no finite-data estimators: plug-in signalling from one or a few occurrences per context is positive in expectation when the true marginals agree, so the contextual fraction is undefined on raw tables, and deficiency over text-valued renderings has no estimator | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and empirical lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. The plug-in signalling of two empirical marginals is positive in expectation when the true marginals agree, so raw tables signal, and the contextual fraction is undefined on them. With one occurrence per context, a non-signalling rank-2 system gives Δ of 0, 2 or 4, with expectation 2: the values [NOTE-654](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-654.md) finds in 51 of the 90 systems behind [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md)'s "69 of the 90 systems signal". The data are author-assigned corpus senses, not judgements. Deficiency over text-valued renderings has no estimator. It does not say signalling is rare in pragmatic judgements, where order effects are themselves signalling. | Active |
| [CLAIM-237](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-237.md) v2 | The first open problem of directed transport is not yet posed: a contextual model is a menu of incompatible experiments, and under the natural order on menus any state-independent classical simulation is dominated automatically, so what is open is only the converse or a deficiency bound | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Blackwell's order compares experiments, each a family of distributions over one parameter. An empirical model has no parameter, and if it is contextual it has no joint distribution, only one per context. Posing [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md)'s first part needs models indexed by situations and an order on menus of experiments. Under the natural order, the preservation direction is automatic for a classical simulation that does not depend on the situation. Granted, because the argument is elementary. It narrows what is open; it does not close it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-238](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-238.md) v2 | Many of the line's defeat conditions cannot in practice be met: the comparative ones are null results with no margin over an observable set the thesis may re-choose, and the possibility theses' are universal negatives that no finite study establishes | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it, though [CASE-029](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-029.md) records the decision rules that were dropped. Three shapes of defeat condition cannot be met. "As well as" is a null result, which needs an equivalence margin and power, and no entry states either. The observables are "not fixed in advance" ([CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)). And the "can" theses are defeated only by "never" or "always", so one construction confirms them and no study refutes them, while what the main thesis needs from them is prevalence and magnitude, which none states. Granted: each point is read off the texts. It does not say the theses are false or untestable in principle. | Active |
| [CLAIM-239](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-239.md) | A defeat condition that says something cannot be done is met by an argument that it cannot, not by a record of failures, so the admissibility and correspondence theses can fail by their own conditions, though no study the programme runs can make them fail | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the fourth point of [CLAIM-238](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-238.md). luria.yaml's blurb for `defeated_if` is "what would defeat the thesis — a kind of result or argument". [CLAIM-077](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-077.md)'s condition and [CLAIM-143](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md)'s second disjunct ("[QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) answered negatively") are met by a showing that the distinctions or correspondences cannot be fixed independently. What the objection gets right is that no finite study meets them, so the programme's experiments do not test these two theses; argument does. Active, because it is read off the rule. | Active |
| [CLAIM-241](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-241.md) v2 | Partial constitution by uptake makes competent participants' uptake a defeasible standard of a communicative kind, not the criterion: where the act's other constituents, such as its institutional conditions, diverge from how even informed participants take it, their verdicts can be wrong, and a standard must say whose competence counts, for which class of acts, and how divided verdicts are combined, which a majority does not | The interlocutor's first refinement at U62 (A240), with its row on [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md), pressed at full strength. [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md) moves from "partly constituted by ... expected uptake" to "the judges ... are the criterion". Partial constitution gives uptake a vote, not the last word, so where the act's other constituents diverge from informed uptake the verdicts can be wrong. The claim also names no rule for combining divided verdicts and no class of acts. Open: answering it means saying whether a defeasible standard re-opens the horn [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md) closed. It does not say uptake is not a standard. | Active |
| [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md) v2 | Read as description, the manuscript's thesis is close to true by definition; read as a criterion, it is a schema until the decision family Q is fixed, and its descriptive defeat condition can test neither reading | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. A distinction no receiver can recover has not survived for anyone, so the descriptive reading is near-analytic. The normative reading leaves which distinctions count to the task family Q, which [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s summary calls "normative and contestable". The defeat condition fixes observables the thesis declines to fix, and tests them descriptively: [CLAIM-085](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-085.md)'s split of normative from descriptive, applied to the thesis rather than to model judges. It does not say the thesis is empty. | Active |
| [CLAIM-245](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-245.md) | Under Contextuality-by-Default, a deterministic context-wise recoding can make a noncontextual signalling source maximally contextual, or turn a contextual source into pure signalling, so per-content signalling is not monotone under such maps and the quantity to bound is joint overlap discrepancy | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Two worked rank-2 systems answer [NOTE-654](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-654.md)'s open question negatively: [THEORY-177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-177.md)'s per-content signalling can rise under deterministic recodings, once the source signals, and CbD contextuality can be created or removed by them. By data processing, the joint overlap discrepancy cannot rise, so that is the quantity [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md)'s second part should name. Granted, because the examples are elementary. It does not say [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) is wrong, which is about no-signalling models. | Active |
| [CLAIM-248](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-248.md) v4 | The founding stimuli (Villon, Henley's Villon, Hofstadter's Marot) and commentary on them are likely in language models' training data, and what a context does to one model need not be what it does to another, so a model's reading of their footing may be recall, and a directional match in one model may not hold in the next | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Agreement in direction is what a model trained on human descriptions of teasing and reproach would show anyway, and Villon, Henley and Hofstadter's Marot are likely in training data, so a model's "interpretation" of them may be recall. [ARG-008](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-008.md) and [CLAIM-085](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-085.md) already bound what model results show about human pragmatics. What is new is that [CLAIM-058](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-058.md)'s validity bar is too low, and the contamination point. Minor. | Active |
| [CLAIM-249](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-249.md) | Comparing characters across realizations needs one group identified on both, which is fixed only up to automorphism, and automorphisms permute the irreducible characters, so "the same character" is relative to a chosen correspondence: the collapse problem again, at the level of the symmetry group | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. To say a visual realization has the same character as a spoken one, the same group element must be named on both sides. Changing that identification by an automorphism α turns χ into χ∘α, and for the cyclic group of order 3 the automorphism g ↦ g² swaps the two nontrivial characters. The transformations the line studies form a semigroup, so the group is a symmetry group the analyst chooses, with its action on each medium fixed independently: [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md)'s anchoring once more. Granted, because the argument is elementary. [CLAIM-132](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-132.md) and [TERM-041](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-041.md) hold neighbouring limits, not this one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-252](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-252.md) | The account does not say which distinctions a translation ought to keep: it says how to tell which ones a rendering kept for stated tasks and receivers, and what ought to be kept is set by the purpose the translation serves | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the criterion horn of [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md). The manuscript calls the choice of observables and decision tasks "normative and contestable (§11)" ([CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s summary), and [CLAIM-085](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-085.md) separates a normative theory of fidelity from a descriptive one. This disclaims the first for the account, so the thesis is not a schema awaiting Q: Q comes from the translation's brief. Active, because it is a statement of what the account claims. Purpose-relative translation norms (skopos theory) are the tradition that states the normative part; they are not held in the record. | Active |
| [CLAIM-253](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md) v2 | The intertwining defects are defined on unobservable interpretive-state spaces, so they are not identified from judgement data, and the commutator identity bounds observed order effects only with a further, unstated readout-intertwining defect | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The commutator identity is correct, but Φ, A and A′ act on interpretive states. [CLAIM-046](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-046.md) says hidden-state models that give identical observations can differ, and a worked case shows two such models with defects 0 and the largest possible, so the defect is not a function of the data. What is observed is responses, and the identity reaches the observed order effect only through a readout defect between outcome spaces, which no draft names. It is distinct from [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md), which is about collapse: this is about identification. | Active |
| [CLAIM-256](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-256.md) | D_obs sums over source contexts only, so a target context outside the image of τ appears in no term: a rendering that adds a relation pays nothing, and a change of cover registers only as loss | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. L_obs and D_obs are sums over source contexts, so a target context that is not the image of one appears in no term. The line says interpreters add relations ([CLAIM-076](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-076.md)) and that a transport can add a distinction ([CLAIM-087](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md)), and D_obs is the one component with a formula ([CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md)). Granted, because it is read off the definition. It does not say no other component could catch an addition, or that additions are distortions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-257](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-257.md) v3 | Observational distortion should be summed over the contexts both covers can host, with the target's new questions asked of the source too, and the questions only one side can decide reported as a separate change of cover, so that a rendering that adds a relation pays for it | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, after [CLAIM-256](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-256.md). D_obs sums over source contexts only, so a target context outside the image of τ is free. Asking the target's new question of the source, where its readers can answer it, puts it in both covers, and an addition then costs. Questions only one side can decide are a change of cover, which [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) makes the line's headline; they are reported, not summed. A proposal: the restatement is a definition, and whether its added term predicts anything is the defeat condition. It does not say additions are distortions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md) v2 | For report fidelity, the decision term should be the positive part of the risk increase on the same decision problem, with losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior; so restated it is directed, counts no improvement as loss, and vanishes for every problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source in Blackwell's order | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, of A86's D_Q after [CLAIM-218](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-218.md). Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺, with r the Bayes risk under the prior π. It is directed and blind to improvement. With Q all finite problems and π all priors, it is zero exactly when V is at least as informative as U in Blackwell's order, by the Bayes form of Blackwell's theorem for finitely many states. A86's D_Q, with the identity on tasks, is its symmetrization. Under report fidelity ([CLAIM-212](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-212.md)) the paired task is the same task, so no scale between tasks is needed. The mathematics is checkable; the claim that this is the right decision term is a proposal. It does not say Q is fixed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-260](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-260.md) | Approximate transports compose into a category only if the distortion obeys a triangle inequality and later kernels are nonexpansive, so the semigroup claim's "category or semigroup" holds for exact kernels, and for approximate ones only under those conditions | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [TERM-008](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-008.md)'s founding sense is a transport that gets "within some eps", and [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md) makes fidelity graded. Kernels always compose, but the composite of an ε₁-transport and an ε₂-transport is an (ε₁ + ε₂)-transport only if the distortion obeys a triangle inequality and the second kernel is nonexpansive. In total variation both hold. [QUESTION-017](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-017.md) holds the triangle inequality open and does not tie it to the category claim. Granted, because it is elementary. It does not say the category claim fails for exact transports or in total variation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-261](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-261.md) v2 | Synchronization of an agent's interests is desirable, but not necessary for acting as one: internal conflict shows a human agent acting while its interests stay divided | The owner's answer to [QUESTION-078](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-078.md). A human agent who acts against a standing temptation acts as one agent while its interests stay divided, so synchronization is not what acting as one consists in. Synchronization is still better when it is available: nothing has to be overridden, and [CLAIM-162](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) says that is why flow is effortless. | Active |
| [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) v2 | Two objects can agree on every probe in a restricted family without being isomorphic, so equivalence under a probe family is coarser than identity unless the family is rich enough | The general content of [CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that it does not rest on [CLAIM-046](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-046.md) and [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md), which are about pragmatic identity. The restricted Yoneda functor is fully faithful exactly when the probe family is dense. A strong generator makes it conservative, which is weaker: a morphism the probes see as invertible is invertible, but objects with isomorphic profiles need not be isomorphic. Matching every probe's marginal leaves the joint unconstrained. The evidential rule is [CLAIM-322](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-322.md)'s. | Active |
| [CLAIM-265](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-265.md) v3 | Local descriptions that disagree are not thereby incompatible: whether they obstruct a joint description is decided only relative to a specified class of admissible correspondences between their observations, and a correspondence admitted only because it removes the disagreement decides nothing | The general content of [CLAIM-143](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the order of tests does not rest on [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md), [CLAIM-004](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-004.md) and [CLAIM-035](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-035.md), which are about translation. Disagreement between local descriptions sorts into a coordinate difference, a structural transformation or a global obstruction, and the sort cannot be made until a class of admissible transition maps is given. Inertial frames ([CASE-039](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-039.md)) show disagreement with no obstruction once the maps are known. | Active |
| [CLAIM-266](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-266.md) v2 | A family of probes that supplies an optimized system's training signal cannot also certify what the system preserves: optimization pushes toward whatever the probes reward, including what they cannot see, so preservation must be shown under probes not used to train it | The general content of [CLAIM-149](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-149.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that it does not rest on [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md)'s account of correspondences in translation. Training against a probe family pushes a system toward whatever the family rewards, including differences it cannot see, so the family is not a certificate of what was preserved. [CASE-041](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-041.md) is a documented instance: a Projected FastGAN trained against ImageNet features matches StyleGAN2's FID, also computed in ImageNet features, while doing worse in CLIP space and with human judges. | Active |
| [CLAIM-267](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-267.md) v3 | Per-step discrepancies between a chain of maps and a reference chain compound through the sensitivity of the later steps, so the same local error can be damped, accumulated or amplified, and closeness at every step can coexist with large end-to-end divergence | The general content of [CLAIM-056](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-056.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the line-neutral recursion does not rest on [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s account of fidelity. It is elementary: with e_(i+1) ≤ L_i e_i + ε_i, the end-to-end error is bounded by the discrepancies weighted by the later Lipschitz constants. Three regimes follow. For stochastic kernels in total variation, contraction coefficients do not exceed one, so amplification needs another metric or a nonlinear, adaptive state. | Active |
| [CLAIM-268](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-268.md) v2 | Model stitching certifies an order of information only in its reconstruction form: a map fitted to reproduce the target layers shows the source representation is at least as informative for every decision on the label, task-loss stitching compares one decision problem through a fixed head, and a failure to stitch is no evidence against sufficiency | The general content of [CLAIM-126](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-126.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the result about stitching does not rest on [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s account of fidelity. Reconstruction-fitted stitching makes the target a garbling of the source given the label, which certifies one direction of Blackwell sufficiency ([THEORY-176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md)). Task-loss stitching ([LIT-850](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-850.md)) compares one decision problem through a fixed head, orders neither representation, and is not invariant under reparametrisation. In both forms a failure says only that no map in the class works. | Active |
| [CLAIM-269](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md) v5 | A regularized linear readout can tell apart only representations that differ in normalized kernel, and kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed, so no such readout supplies a distinction beyond that symmetry | The general content of [CLAIM-193](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-193.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the linear result does not rest on [CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), whose realist reading is about communicative identity. What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of the normalized kernel ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)). Kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed (THEORY-004, THEORY-723). An inner product beyond that is a stipulation ([THEORY-018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md)). And spectral degeneracy does not identify the symmetry ([THEORY-019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md)). These are proved results for learned representations. | Active |
| [CLAIM-270](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-270.md) v2 | Retaining information about where a Markov chain started and staying close to the starting distribution are different properties: a chain can forget its initial state while its distribution stays far from where it began, so convergence is not preservation and losing information about the origin is not degradation | The general content of [CLAIM-081](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-081.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the distinction does not rest, through [CLAIM-056](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-056.md), on [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s account of fidelity. I(U_0; U_n) and D[P(U_n), P(U_0)] answer different questions. A contractive chain loses information about its initial state while converging to a stationary distribution that can be far from the start. The data-processing inequality bounds the first and says nothing about the second. | Active |
| [CLAIM-272](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-272.md) v2 | Giving every member an equal budget of actions does not equalize their influence: coordination is one route, letting a member's plan direct other members' actions, so a cap on self-allocation constrains action and not authority | A8 §3 on the owner's r/place case. Every account had the same cooldown, a ban on self-allocation at the level of pixels, yet "a participant who creates a successful design template might have almost no direct pixel- writing capacity beyond any ordinary user, yet exercise enormous influence". A8: "Reddit's software imposed a cooldown and common action budget, but did not give participants equal *effective* influence." It qualifies [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md): the budget constrains moves, and endorsement moves authority. It does not say the inequality is illegitimate. | Active |
| [CLAIM-273](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-273.md) v6 | A maintained r/place artwork copied from an off-canvas design is a dissipative structure in Prigogine's structural sense, order held only by a sustained flow of repair against rival coalitions and against unaffiliated placement whose rate falls over the event, but its order is imported from the design and not born of an instability | The owner, on reading Wu and Silva's finding that lasting artworks are those whose coalitions keep working under continual overwriting: "sounds like there's likely a connection to dissipative structure here". It holds for half of Prigogine's criterion ([NOTE-424](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-424.md)): an open system kept from the state it would drift to by a sustained flow, here of placements. The flow works against two sources of corruption. One is rival coalitions. The other is unaffiliated placement, a real decay whose rate falls over the event (version 2, the owner's correction, [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md)). It fails for the other half, since a copied artwork's order comes from its design, not from an instability (CASE-079; Adams et al. corroborate). No thermodynamic quantity is defined. | Active |
| [CLAIM-275](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-275.md) v2 | An intervention can come before the interpretation it makes available, so in an organization of processes meaning, policy and influence can co-evolve, and none of them is upstream of the others in every case | A4 §6, on the record's two accounts of emotion, Frijda's appraisal upstream of action readiness and Barrett's construction, and the owner's two replies at U5: "yes, exactly" to "meaning, policy, and influence can co-evolve", and "so much yes" to "An operator may act not because it already possesses an interpretation, but because its intervention creates the conditions under which a particular interpretation becomes available." The first filing left both out. It does not say interpretation never comes first. | Active |
| [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md) v4 | Durable authority among an organization's processes need not be a primitive: trust can be the temporal regularity of endorsement that policies earn by being right often, and the same loop entrenches whatever gained influence early | The owner's objection at U5 to A4's call to keep "persistent authority structures" distinct from "transient endorsement updates": "I'd expect persistent authority to be an emergent property here as 'right a lot' policies become distinguished into 'trusted' policies." A5 granted it. Momentary endorsement, established trust and institutionalized authority are regimes of one process, set by how slowly endorsers forget. A5 added the converse: the same loop turns an early lead into durable authority. The claim does not say which of the two a given organization does. | Active |
| [CLAIM-279](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-279.md) v5 | Whether an intervention stabilizes or destabilizes a pattern is relative to a policy and a frame, so denoiser, critic and re-noiser are regimes an operator falls into, not kinds of operator | The owner at U3 proposed operators that may "*re*noise the region it has influence over e.g. because it disagrees with the direction of the current work", and at U5 that named operator types are "just different regimes in the dynamics of our general process", with niches emerging. A5 granted it. A8 grounded it in the owner's r/place case: restoring a pixel is denoising for the group whose image it is and destruction for the group overwriting it. The claim does not say specialization always emerges. | Active |
| [CLAIM-280](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) v2 | A pattern can persist while every constituent is replaced and some constituents work against it, as a high-turnover regime of damage and repair, so the persistence of a product and the persistence of the organization producing it are separate facts | A8 §4 and §9, on the owner's r/place case. An artwork defended for days has its pixels repeatedly replaced, its defenders come and go, and its attackers keep working, yet the image stays recognizable. Its stability is continuous activity, not the absence of it. A8: "the distinction between a persistent product and a persistent producer". An image can outlast the coalition behind it, and a coalition can outlast the images it makes. The claim does not say that the pattern, or the coalition, is a self. | Active |
| [CLAIM-282](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md) | Forbidding self-endorsement does not stop an operator from amplifying its own authority: once endorsement can carry authority more than one hop, reciprocal and cyclic endorsements recycle it, and only one-hop allocation within an epoch makes an operator's authority independent of its own endorsements | A2's own analysis of the owner's U2 design, conceded in the exchange and checked here. With damped recursive delegation (a PageRank-like fixed point), two operators that endorse each other pass authority back and forth, so each one's authority depends on its own outgoing endorsements even though neither endorses itself. With one-hop allocation from budgets fixed independently of outgoing endorsements, that dependence is exactly zero. No accounting rule removes the slower route: an operator can change its authority by changing what others endorse. | Active |
| [CLAIM-283](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) v2 | The precedence a motive claims over action and the authority the rest of the organization grants it are different quantities: a motive can claim control without receiving it, and be granted control it does not claim | A4 §2, reading Frijda through the record: "control precedence also suggests a useful addition to our parameterization", a priority p_i claimed by a process, which "is not the same as granted influence I_i. An operator can urgently demand control without receiving it. That distinction between *claimed precedence* and *endorsed authority* may be essential to modeling internal conflict." It joins [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md) to the endorsement scheme. It does not say which wins. | Active |
| [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) v6 | A self, in the self-governing sense, is a historically continuous organization of processes that takes part in governing the conditions of its own persistence, differentiation and transformation, not merely one that persists | A10 §11's central hypothesis, reached after the owner asked at U10 for a research programme on a constitutive theory of selfhood. It treats the endogeneity of governance as the distinguishing mark: the organization takes part in changing how it will operate, which CLAIM-485 locates in revising its governing standards rather than in allocating authority among its processes. A11 named its falsifier. "Self" is in [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s self-governing sense, with persisting and integrated senses nearby, and not the subject sense. None of the entries it is set against objects to it as stated: it disclaims the will CLAIM-116 denies, the subject sense of CLAIM-165 and a boundary test (CLAIM-194), and CLAIM-288 undercuts ARG-015, the sufficiency-test route to it, not the claim. | Active |
| [CLAIM-287](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) v4 | What persists when a self persists through inactivity is the capacity to reinstate an organization, not its continuous running, and continuity of that kind can branch and merge, so it is not an identity relation | A6 §7 and A10 §4.3. A6 separated activation continuity, organizational continuity and policy continuity, and put identity in the second: "A dormant coalition can remain available for reactivation because learned parameters, memory traces, and endorsement structures persist." A10 added that continuity of descent "is not automatically an equivalence relation. Organizational histories can branch, merge, and partially overlap." It sits beside [CLAIM-161](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md), which asks for a coherence measure conserved along a system's own trajectory, and qualifies it for gaps. Its second half is Parfit's branching argument (THEORY-447) applied to organizational continuity. It uses [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s persisting sense. | Active |
| [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) v7 | In a population whose operators each maximize an objective the modeller fixed, the norms the organization appears to maintain are set by the modeller, not by the organization: they can become its goals through their role in selecting what persists, but it does not produce or revise them | The record's objection, raised by no one in the exchange. A2 gives each operator an objective J_i, its evaluation of the collective decision, and A7 and A10 propose sufficiency tests run on such populations. Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde hold that systems optimizing an externally fixed function are not models of agency ([NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md), C5), and Di Paolo (2005) that a system's norms must be norms for the system. The objection undermines the evidence route; it does not refute the thesis. It is answered if the operators' objectives are themselves produced and revised by the organization. | Active |
| [CLAIM-289](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-289.md) | Non-stochastic strings stay non-stochastic under total recursive models: their minimal randomness deficiency agrees with the finite-set one to within O(log n) in argument and value | The step that [THEORY-260](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-260.md)'s promotion (version 2) names as the record's own: carrying [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md)'s non-stochastic strings, proved for finite-set models, to total recursive function models through Propositions B.1(b) and B.2(b) with Remark B.3. Remark B.3 asserts wholesale that every result of the paper extends to total functions up to a logarithmic term. This writes the extension out for this one result. It holds at O(log n) precision only, and does not reach [LIT-229](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-229.md)'s sophistication, which is defined at constant precision. | Active |
| [CLAIM-290](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md) | A positive-definite kernel's minimal realizations are unique up to a unitary, and two finite representation matrices with the same centred Gram matrix differ by a translation and an orthogonal map | The record's own proofs of two steps that [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) rests on and that its sources state without proof. (a) Jorgensen & Tian's Cor. 1.35: minimal realizations of a positive-definite kernel are unique up to a unitary. The book leaves this "as an exercise", and [NOTE-829](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-829.md) supplied the book's own proof of Thm 4.35, transferred. (b) The finite case that [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md) §5.3 states as known: XXᵀ = YYᵀ implies Y = XQ with Q orthogonal, with no assumption that the rows span R^d. With centring this becomes a translation and an orthogonal map. It does not say Q is unique, which fails when the rank is below d. | Active |
| [CLAIM-291](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-291.md) | The adjoint of a square-integrable integral operator is the integral operator with the conjugate-transposed kernel | The record's own step, written down in [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md) and marked there as not the Riesz article's, which covers matrices and bounded operators only. For a kernel k in L²(μ⊗ν), the operator (Tf)(x) = ∫ k(x,y) f(y) dν(y) from L²(ν) to L²(μ) has adjoint (T*g)(y) = ∫ k̄(x,y) g(x) dμ(x), by Cauchy–Schwarz and Fubini. So T is self-adjoint, when μ = ν, exactly when k(x,y) = k̄(y,x) almost everywhere. It does not say where the symmetry of k comes from, which is [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md)'s question, and it is not claimed for kernels that are not square-integrable. | Active |
| [CLAIM-292](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-292.md) | Retrieval that depends on current belief is not a bias in itself: adaptive search can be rational when inference accounts for how the evidence was selected, and calling a search biased needs a standard outside the search | Granted against [CLAIM-301](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-301.md), as A21 insisted ("That counter is essential. Without it, we'd be using 'anchoring' as a blanket criticism of adaptive search."), and said again at A20 §5, A21 §4 and A23 V.E. Sequential experimental design chooses its next observation by its current belief and is not thereby biased. | Active |
| [CLAIM-293](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md) | The topology of a support graph does not fix how a conclusion should be revised when one of its supports fails: two records with the same edges can carry evidence of different strength and call for different revisions | A6's compensating-evidence case ([CASE-089](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-089.md)), granted against reading [CLAIM-295](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-295.md) as saying a graph of justifications is enough. Two pieces of evidence support H in both worlds. Discount the first, and posterior odds are 20:1 in one world and 1.1:1 in the other. `rests_on` and `grounds` record that support exists, not how much. | Active |
| [CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md) v2 | Two inquiry histories can agree on every current conclusion and still call for different revisions of it, so a current marginal belief is not a sufficient state for updating on evidence about what it depended on | A5's central claim, made exact by A8's construction ([CASE-093](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-093.md)) and checked here. Two joint distributions over a hypothesis H and a condition C share P(H) = 0.9; learning C = 1 sends one to 1.0 and the other to 0.8. Keeping only the marginal merges histories that need different updates. It does not say a full posterior falls short ([CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md)), or that a dependency graph is the fix ([CLAIM-293](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-296](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-296.md) v2 | What a system has, what it knows it has, and what it can deploy within a task's deadline are different, and the last is a relation among the resource, the agent, its environment, the task, the deadline and the cue, not a property of any one of them | A18's first candidate, from the owner's EMT case ([CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)): the drug was stocked, the EMT knew it, and it could not be found before the medic moved on. "If I can't find it, it isn't there" is false of the inventory and right of the decision. [TERM-055](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md) names the relation. A19 added the cue: the same memory under a different request may retrieve it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md) v5 | When an operator's authority is updated by how well it performs on the interpretation it helped make dominant, the coupled meaning and influence of an organization can amplify an initial interpretive advantage without any gain in fidelity to independent evidence | A22's narrow claim and A23 VIII.E's central hypothesis, from the owner's U22: connect retrieval-mediated anchoring to the record's distributed agent as dual meaning and influence canvases ([CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md), [TERM-053](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-053.md)). Its existence is shown in the linearization of a model of the kind in CASE-092 (CLAIM-330); the nonlinear model is unanalysed (QUESTION-100). If the influence field adds nothing to ordinary adaptive retrieval, the objection once filed as CLAIM-278, now ARG-036, stands against it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-299](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-299.md) | Decision sufficiency, historical accountability and correctness are three properties of a record of inquiry, and each can hold while the other two fail | A8's "small mathematical structure", with A5's "Epistemic traceability and epistemic sufficiency are different properties". Shown by construction: a sufficient posterior without history ([CASE-082](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-082.md)), a perfectly accountable record that is wrong ([CASE-084](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-084.md)), a current marginal that is right and cannot be revised ([CASE-093](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-093.md)). [CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) and [CLAIM-190](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-190.md) hold neighbouring points about measuring an argument. This names the three predicates so the others can say which they mean. | Active |
| [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md) | A state sufficient for a family of decisions under a model makes the rest of an inquiry's history worthless for those decisions, and it can stop being sufficient when a source is discredited, the model is revised or the decisions change | A10's answer to the owner's U10, with A8's fourth case and A10's normal constructions ([CASE-082](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-082.md), [CASE-087](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-087.md)). Under a fixed, correctly specified model a sufficient posterior makes the history redundant for those decisions. The same sample mean that sufficed cannot say which reading remains when one instrument is discredited, or test a mixture. Sufficiency was always relative to the model and the family. [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) says the same of individuation by target; this says it of a retained state over time. | Active |
| [CLAIM-302](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md) | Equivalence under feasible tests can be much coarser than statistical equivalence: there are ensembles almost disjoint from uniform that no polynomial-size test tells apart from it, and efficiently samplable ensembles of this kind exist if pseudorandom generators do | A15's witness for "Complexity changes what we mean by an observable", which the owner asked to have developed at U15, corrected by the reading of Goldreich (NOTE of 2026-10-15). [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) says agreement on a restricted probe family is coarser than identity; feasibility gives a restriction that is forced, not chosen. The separation itself is unconditional: a counting argument gives ensembles supported on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no circuit of size 2^(n/8) tells from uniform. Only an efficiently samplable witness needs an assumption, and a secure pseudorandom generator supplies one. All of it is asymptotic, about ensembles indexed by n. | Active |
| [CLAIM-304](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md) | A rendering can keep a distinction recoverable in principle and make it infeasible to recover: if pseudorandom generators exist, a uniformly random bit can be encoded so that an unbounded receiver recovers it except with probability at most 2⁻⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾, while no efficient receiver does non-negligibly better than chance | A14's first failure mode, computational inaccessibility, and A18's fourth candidate: "Recoverable in principle ≠ recoverable within budget." [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md) shows a garbling can help a bounded receiver. This is the other direction: a nearly lossless rendering can defeat every efficient one. The construction is the record's, from [CLAIM-302](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md)'s witness; A18 asked for one and warned against "a vague appeal to an inverse being hard". | Active |
| [CLAIM-305](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-305.md) | Resolving a singularity by blow-up reparametrizes the states and adds no observation, so it cannot make indistinguishable states distinguishable: every point over a singular point gives the same distribution, and the Fisher information can stay degenerate there; what the resolution buys is a normal form for the divergence, and so the learning coefficient | The owner's LEGO monograph says, in Part I (chapters 4, 6, 7, 9, the Overview and "Definitions and Theorems"), that blow-up "restores identifiability", "introduces new observables" and makes the Fisher information non-degenerate, and maps it onto splitting a LEGO bin. The pulled-back model is p(x \| π(u)), a function of u only through π(u), so every point of the exceptional divisor gives the distribution of the singular point. In p(x \| a, b) = N(ab, 1), the chart a = u, b = uv gives mean u²v and a Fisher matrix of zero all along u = 0. Splitting a bin is refining the observable, which can separate states. [MOM-CLM-099](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-099.md) records that the monograph uses "blow-up" in three senses; this records why the analogy cannot hold in any of them. | Active |
| [CLAIM-307](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-307.md) | Retrieval pressure and evidence are different criteria for carving a category, and they move in opposite directions with copy count: evidence that a distinction exists grows with its copies, the search a bin saves shrinks with them, so the bins a deadline forces are often the ones the data least supports | From [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md), which reads the owner's LEGO parable ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) against a formalism that cited it with the sign reversed. [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) says when a distinction is real enough to name. Its evidence grows with the number of copies. The parable says when a distinction must be built to act in time: a single brick among similar ones. Expected search falls as copies grow. The two answer different questions, "is it there?" and "can it be reached in time?", and come apart in both directions. MOM's table was re-run here and reproduced, and a simulation of the search agrees. | Active |
| [CLAIM-309](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-309.md) | How good a mixture is and how discriminable it is from its diluent come apart: under linear mixing a smoothie's distance from milk only shrinks as milk is added, so a preference that rises and then falls with milk is over the ratio and cannot be a d′, and the signal-detection reading of the owner's smoothie line reverses one of its directions | The smoothie note in the owner's LEGO monograph reads the owner's line ([CASE-096](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-096.md)) as signal detection. Milk is the noise, "Less Good" is d′ falling as the mixture approaches milk, and "More Good" is d′ rising as a little milk is added. Under linear mixing the mixture's taste is (1 − f)s + f·m, and its distance from milk is (1 − f)\|s − m\|. That falls monotonically from the first drop, so discriminability from milk cannot rise and then fall. The note's own first model is right: goodness is a single-peaked function of the ratio, which is a preference, not a discriminability. [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md) found the same kind of reversal in the formal reading of the LEGO parable. MOM's record never mentions the smoothie note. | Active |
| [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) v2 | Sorting schemes over objects with determinate properties never conflict as descriptions, since the product of any sortings refines them all; they conflict as arrangements, since a fixed number of bins realizes one partition when each item is stored once, and which costs least depends on what is searched for and on what stands out within a bin | What is directionally right in the owner's LEGO monograph, as Mathematics of Meaning graded it. Its contextuality claim is empty: any sortings of bricks share a joint refinement ([MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md)), and the events they generate stay Boolean ([MOM-ARG-047](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md)). Its intuition that builders cannot share a sorting is true of arrangements. One set of bins realizes one partition, the product may need more bins than there are, and the cheapest choice depends on what each builder searches for and on what stands out within a bin ([CASE-095](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md)). The disagreement is a trade, not a failure of global truth. Sorting on one attribute also turns a search for a combination of features into a search for one feature within each bin, which Treisman and Gelade (LIT-1082, read) show is the difference between a serial scan and one found at a glance. | Active |
| [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) | A search cut off before an exhaustive pass can establish absence when the arrangement certifies that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item: a sorted table answers non-membership in a logarithmic number of probes, and the Threshold Algorithm stops early with its answer proved, so absence needs a certificate about the remainder, not exhaustion; similarity search in high dimension is where no such certificate exists | Filed at the owner's request, from the database readings set against [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry: presence by one find, absence "only by exhausting the collection". Sorted order and the Threshold Algorithm each establish absence from part of the collection, because the arrangement bounds what the rest can hold. That meets [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s own defeat condition, and the claim is conceded: [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) restates it. Where the arrangement gives no bound, as in similarity search in high dimension, [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry stands. | Active |
| [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) v2 | "If I can't find it, it isn't there" asserts operational unavailability, that the item will not be put to use before the deadline, not absence: a search that fails by the deadline establishes unavailability outright, and licenses absence only with a certificate that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item, from exhaustion, from an invariant of the arrangement, or from a closed-world default | Restates [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) at the owner's request, after [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) showed that absence can be established without exhausting a collection. The owner's own wording in [CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md), "it may as well not be there", is hyperbole for operational availability ([TERM-055](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md)), not a claim about inventory. Read so, the rule reports an outcome and needs no default. [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s analysis survives as the account of the literal reading: what a failed search must be joined with before it licenses absence. The gap between the two readings is [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s Bayes term, and it matters when the statement is passed to someone who will act on presence. | Active |
| [CLAIM-313](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-313.md) v2 | A fixed number of bins realizes one partition only when each item is stored once: with copies, overlapping partitions coexist, as hashing-based similarity search stores each item in many partitions and pays for it in space, so sortings conflict as arrangements only under a one-copy constraint, which binds bricks but not index entries | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on locality-sensitive hashing (Indyk and Motwani 1998; Andoni, Laarhoven, Razenshteyn and Waingarten 2017) set against [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md)'s premise that "a set of k bins realizes one partition of the collection at a time". That holds when each item is in one place. An index can hold many copies, and hashing-based similarity indexes do exactly that, trading the space of the copies against query time on an exact curve. It narrows [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) to collections whose items cannot be copied, which includes the LEGO case; it does not touch the claim about descriptions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-316](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-316.md) v2 | A person's drive profile is time-indexed: who drives changes with state, such as hungry or sated and stressed or calm, with task and with regime | Split from [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the first of the owner's two parts of 2026-10-11, "'who drives' isn't a constant", stated on its own. It is argued from the drive-profile term and the will line's account of which regime is effective, and no observation the record holds estimates a person's drive profile over successive windows, so it is interpretive. The microbiome part, which the reviews support, stays in [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md). | Active |
| [CLAIM-318](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-318.md) | Within a shared observational scenario, exact structure-preserving symmetries are the invertible members of a nested family of stochastic transports, and among Markov kernels between finite sets the invertible ones are the permutation matrices, so the invertible core is the relabellings, a groupoid in which objects joined by an arrow have isomorphic automorphism groups | Split from [CLAIM-103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-103.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the nesting and its invertible core, stated on their own so that their warrant can be. A110 §25 nests exact symmetries inside structure-compatible transports inside stochastic communicative transports, within a shared scenario, and the exact symmetries are the invertible ones. For Markov kernels between finite sets, a stochastic matrix with a stochastic inverse is a permutation matrix, because a nonnegative matrix with a nonnegative inverse is monomial, so the invertible core is the relabellings. In that groupoid an invertible u : A → B gives Aut(A) ≅ Aut(B), which corrects A198 §8. It does not say what symmetries are for: that they supply the yardstick for non-symmetric transports is [CLAIM-103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-103.md)'s, and interpretive. | Active |
| [CLAIM-319](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-319.md) | Over a scenario of n contexts in an odd cycle, changing the support of one context takes the contextual fraction from 1 to 0 while the other n − 1 contexts and every marginal are kept exactly, at a weighted observational distortion of 1/n, so within a scenario the fraction's Lipschitz constant against that distortion is at least n; and any change of global extension needs a contextual model on one side | Split from [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the derivation that claim called "decisive and checkable", stated on its own. For odd n, an n-cycle of ±1 observables in which every context anticorrelates is strongly contextual; making one context correlate gives a model with a global distribution. The two agree on n − 1 contexts and on every marginal, differ by total variation 1 in the last, and so lie at weighted D_obs = 1/n with contextual fractions 1 and 0. For n = 3 it is [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md) with one observable relabelled. It answers how small the local change can be; it says nothing about whether any data are contextual. | Active |
| [CLAIM-320](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-320.md) | Within one fixed measurement scenario, two no-signalling empirical models can agree on all but one of their contexts and on every single-observable marginal while their contextual fractions are 1 and 0, so keeping most local judgement distributions does not fix their global compatibility | Split from [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the possibility that claim's headline needs, shown by the pair it lost and recovered in [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md). On the cover {AB, BC, AC} with binary outcomes, the parity triangle at 1/2 per allowed outcome is no-signalling and strongly contextual, with contextual fraction 1. Change only S_AC to {(0,0), (1,1)}: two contexts and every marginal are unchanged, and the model now extends to a global distribution, with fraction 0. It is an existence result by construction, and the weights are stipulated. It does not say reconstruction chains do this, which is [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)'s thesis and interpretive, and the context that changes moves by a total-variation distance of 1. | Active |
| [CLAIM-321](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-321.md) v4 | In text-to-image diffusion models each condition of a prompt can be met while their conjunction or relational binding fails: benchmarks find single objects rendered almost always and spatial relations and attribute binding failing most, and composing by adding scores does worst on relations | Split from [CLAIM-123](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical part of that claim, that each condition can be met while their conjunction or relational binding fails, documented by GenEval, T2I-CompBench and T2I-CompBench++, by Attend-and-Excite's "catastrophic neglect", and by Composable Diffusion losing to an energy-based baseline on relations. It corroborates [CLAIM-123](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md)'s derivation without carrying it, and does not say what causes the failures. | Active |
| [CLAIM-322](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-322.md) v2 | Agreement under a probe family is evidence that two objects share structure only to the degree that the family was chosen independently of the comparison and is evaluated on cases it was not chosen on, so a family selected to make two objects look alike shows only that it can be selected | Split from [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): its evidential half, stated on its own so that its warrant can be. [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md)'s exact half shows that agreement on a restricted probe family does not fix identity; this claim draws the rule for reading such agreement as evidence. It is an argument, not a theorem, so it is interpretive. It does not say which probes to choose, or that held-out probes are neutral. | Active |
| [CLAIM-323](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-323.md) v2 | Where source and rendering are experiments about one common situation, a rendering that depends on the situation other than through the source is not a garbling of it and can be incomparable with it in Blackwell's order: with Z uniform on {1, 2, 3}, a source that tells whether Z = 1 and a rendering that tells whether Z = 3 each have the lower 0–1 risk on one of the problems of saying whether Z = 1 and whether Z = 3, so neither dominates | Split from [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the worked case that objection uses, stated on its own so that its warrant can be. Over a common situation Z uniform on three values, U reports whether Z = 1 and V whether Z = 3. V is not a garbling of U, since given U = 0 it still varies with Z, and the risks on "say whether Z = 3" (0 from V, 1/3 from U) and "say whether Z = 1" (the reverse) show neither experiment dominates. It is an existence result by construction. It does not say this is the normal translation case, which is [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md)'s reading and is interpretive. | Active |
| [CLAIM-324](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-324.md) v2 | In the What Survives Translation? exchange, the manuscript drafted straight from the crystallized argument changed the thesis with no turn arguing the move and dropped 24 of that argument's items, none on request, and the second crystallized argument announced its change of question but left items out without saying which had dissolved and which were lost | Split from [CLAIM-178](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-178.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the documented case on which that claim's normative conclusion rests, scoped to the one exchange it comes from. The evidence is the workbench reconstructions of that exchange (2026/10/09/025539, 2026/10/10/040457). One exchange, reconstructed turn by turn by the record's own readers; it says nothing about drafts in general. | Active |
| [CLAIM-325](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-325.md) | The behavioural data the record has read show no contextuality proper: none of the five kinds of data Dzhafarov, Zhang and Kujala re-analyse is contextual, Wang et al. test none of their 90 language systems for it, and no documented test of pragmatic or meaning judgements finds it at adequate power | Split from [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical premise of that objection's dilemma, which [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) conceded. | [CLAIM-326](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-326.md) v5 | With losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior, the positive part of the Bayes-risk increase on the same decision problem, D⁺_Q(U → V; π), is directed, is zero from a garbling back to its source, vanishes for every finite problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source in Blackwell's order, over finitely many states and a source whose outcome space is standard Borel, and has A86's D_Q, with the identity on tasks, as its symmetrization | Split from [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the properties of the restated decision term, which [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md) called "elementary and checkable", stated on their own so that their warrant can be. Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺. A garbling never gains; with Q all finite problems and π all priors, the term vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by the Bayes form of Blackwell's theorem for finitely many states ([THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md)); it is directed; and A86's D_Q is its symmetrization. It does not say this is the right decision term, which is [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md)'s proposal, and it does not state the prior-free relation to Le Cam's deficiency. | Active |
| [CLAIM-328](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-328.md) v3 | When the continuities that ordinarily come bundled in a collective (legal franchise, civic role, interpersonal transmission, narrative and place) are separated, several later collectives can each be a genuine successor of the earlier one in a different respect, without any of them, or the earlier collective, having branched in numerical identity | A4's H5 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, in its weak form, on the Washington Senators. | [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md) | In the coupled meaning–influence model linearized at its symmetric state, with each field stable alone and nonnegative couplings, the coupling destabilizes symmetry exactly when βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ): only the loop can do it, and the direction that grows mixes meaning and authority | A14 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, checked. For J = [[α, β], [γ, δ]] with nonnegative entries and α, δ < 1, the leading eigenvalue exceeds 1 iff βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ). If either coupling is zero the eigenvalues are α and δ. The leading eigenvector is (β, λ+ − α), positive in both components. A partial answer to [QUESTION-100](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-100.md)'s "when the symmetric state is unstable", for the linearization only; it says nothing about the nonlinear attractors or about fidelity. | Active |
| [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) v9 | A level of organization has a temporal facet as well as a compositional one: higher-level variables are characteristically slower and longer-lived than the activity that produces them, though slowness is a mark of a level and not its definition | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "'higher level' doesn't just mean in terms of abstractions over abstractions, we should also expect 'higher level' effects to be on slower timescales than 'lower level' effects."
