| [CLAIM-333](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md) | Measuring every relevant variable is necessary but not sufficient for a Granger-causal analysis to say anything about interventions: the intervention must also be an isolated exogenous change and no influence may act within one sampling step, and then Granger noncausality implies no intervention effect and the effect is identified from the observational predictor, but a Granger-causal relation is still only potentially causal | The record's answer to [NOTE-010](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-010.md)'s C5, "if all relevant variables are measured, Granger- and Pearl-type analyses coincide", which the ΦID review asserts without conditions. Checked by hand and by simulation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-334](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-334.md) | Granger causation from a macro variable to the micro variables it supervenes on, Seth's downward Granger causation, is not evidence of a macro-to-micro intervention effect, even with every micro variable measured: supervenience leaves no intervention on the macro variable that holds its micro base fixed at the same time | Seth measures downward causation as Granger causation from the flock's centre of mass to each boid, and calls it "ontologically innocent" ([THEORY-703](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-703.md)). | [CLAIM-335](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-335.md) v3 | Transfer entropy measures directed predictive improvement, not information flow: as a conditional mutual information it is the source's unique information about the target's next value plus its synergy with the target's past, so it can credit a source with a bit the source carries only jointly and read zero from sources that jointly fix the target, and conditioning on more series does not remove the synergy | The record's position on whether transfer entropy measures information flow. Both papers' examples were recomputed exactly. This is a different failure from [CLAIM-333](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md)'s, prediction against intervention. It leaves transfer entropy standing as a predictive quantity. | Active |
| [CLAIM-339](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-339.md) v3 | A judgement–observation loop cut off from action loses one route for evidence it did not select, and the free-energy principle's reason for minimizing surprise, that a persisting system must keep its states in bounds, needs action on the world, though a loop can confirm itself with action available too | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, narrowed at A4. Friston et al. (2010) say active sampling is "mandated by ergodic arguments based on the very existence of adaptive agents", and the enactive account puts a system's own norms in its capacity to act against tendencies toward its viability boundary. Kübler and Birbaumer's extinction hypothesis is the empirical form. As first filed it said a loop without action has a self-confirming minimum. [NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md) shows the minimum arises with action available, so the counter now claims only that losing action removes one source of evidence the loop did not select. [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) answers it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md) | Scoring operators on predictions committed before the evidence is not by itself Regime B: in the linearized operator model the coupling of interpretation to endorsement has the sign of κ′ − κ̄, so commitment removes capture only when the interpretation bends the reading of the evidence no more than it bends the predictions, and it keeps the learning that revising after the evidence would lose | The formal question [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md) asked, answered in [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s linearization ([CASE-106](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-106.md)): is committing predictions before the evidence equivalent to Regime B? No. The coupling γ is 4ηs(κ′ − κ̄), where κ̄ is how far the shared meaning bends the committed predictions and κ′ how far it bends the reading of the evidence. It is corrective, null or capturing as κ′ is below, at or above κ̄. Strong correction can fail by oscillation when \|βγ\| ≥ 1 − αδ. Revising predictions after the evidence sets γ = 0 but also stops authority from tracking who predicts well. Linear, at the symmetric state, for squared-error scoring. | Active |
| [CLAIM-341](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-341.md) v3 | The loop that keeps a lucid agent's model in touch with what it models runs between judgement and observation: each judgement reshapes the observer whose later observations it then judges, and action on the world is not part of that loop, so active inference's action–perception cycle misplaces where the agent is active | The owner's, U1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: Friston's free-energy approach is "generally correct, but the cybernetic model is wrong"; action can be cut out of the loop, which decomposes into "Judgement (qua measurement that generates interpretations) <--> Observation". At U2 the owner held that the pragmatic-transport and will-organization models are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". | [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) v3 | What keeps a judgement–observation loop from confirming itself is evidence whose arrival or scoring does not pass through the interpretation it tests; action is one source of such evidence, not a necessary one, and a loop that selects its own evidence can lock in with action available | The assistant's synthesis, A3 and A4 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, filed at the owner's request at U5. Three results the record already holds. [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md): capture in the operator model needs both arrows of [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and scoring operators independently of the dominant interpretation removes it. [CLAIM-141](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-141.md): a loop always has a distributional fixed point, so what binds it is a constraint that prescribes marginals. [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) ([NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md)): an active-inference agent locks in with action available, because its own sampling policy withholds the evidence that would correct it. | [CLAIM-343](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-343.md) | For three or more parts, no ΦID can use a redundancy function that both satisfies the identity axiom and yields nonnegative atoms, because on the Williams–Beer lattice the two are inconsistent from three sources up; a ΦID verdict on three or more parts therefore rests on which axiom the analyst drops, and should name it | The record's answer to the gap left by the PID filing: no held measure gave ΦID an identity-respecting redundancy for more than two sources. The record's measures split the difference: I_min keeps atoms nonnegative by calling independent copied bits redundant, and Ince's I_ccs keeps an independent-sources identity and reports a −1-bit atom ([THEORY-714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-714.md)). Two-part ΦID is untouched. | Active |
| [CLAIM-344](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-344.md) v3 | Resolve is a maintained organization of precedence, commitment and revision that keeps a temporally extended policy effective across changes in locally dominant evaluations while keeping the capacity to revise it; mere slowness or persistence is not resolve | The owner's frame, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "I think emergence of "resolve" could be an interesting frame within which to examine our will-organization framework." | [CLAIM-345](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-345.md) | Equal controllability rank does not fix the cost of control: for x_{t+1} = x_t + b·u the least quadratic effort for a displacement Δ is Δ²/b², unbounded as b → 0 while the system stays controllable, and in general the least effort is Δxᵀ W_T^† Δx, set by the Gramian and not by its rank | A9 §2 and A12's Proposition 1 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, the step the owner's U9 "controllability of a system isn't binary" needs. For a scalar step x_{t+1} = x_t + b·u the cheapest input costs Δ²/b², so two systems that are both controllable can differ in cost by any factor. The general statement is the minimum-energy formula with the controllability Gramian. A9: "This is already a standard result from linear control theory." Proved here because the record holds no source for it. The sharp edge: the cost is relative to a fixed input norm, and rescaling the input makes every b cost the same, so comparing costs across systems needs inputs in common units. | Active |
| [CLAIM-346](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-346.md) | Feasibility, aggregation and epistemic coordination are independent obstructions to an organization's realizing its demands: each can occur with the other two absent | Owner-seeded, U36 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: Arrow's theorem, then cryptography and "the two generals problem". A36 placed them: "Arrow's theorem belongs in the theory of endorsement, not directly in the geometry of feasible updates", and the two generals add "epistemic frustration". Three elementary constructions, each with one obstruction and not the others, are given in the body. The sharp edge: the independence is relative to fixing the demands as the constituents' own acceptance conditions; that no remedy for one removes another is A36's further reading, argued in the body and not part of the claim. | Active |
| [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) v3 | Frustration among an organization's demands is an ordinal fact before it is a quantity: the jointly satisfiable sets of demands form a downward-closed complex whose minimal non-faces are the minimal conflicts, relief is strict enlargement of that complex for the same declared demands, reorganizations that relieve different conflicts are incomparable, and dropping or suppressing a demand is not relief | The owner's correction, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "We can do quite a lot with access to an ordering, even if it doesn't give us a true measure." A37 granted it ("I agree with your correction") and built the acceptance sets, their intersection and the compatibility complex. Corrected here: acceptance conditions sit on attainable outcomes, a demand's form depends on whether it demands improvement or maintenance, and A37's weak-preference sets fail only as representations of improvement demands. The definitional facts are shown in the body, including that every pair of demands can be jointly improvable while the triple is not. The sharp edge: relief compares complexes for the same declared demands, so a reorganization that deletes a demand is not compared at all, and two reorganizations can be incomparable. It is the move [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) made for translation, in a new line. | Active |
| [CLAIM-348](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) v4 | No coarse-graining is normatively adequate in general because it preserves stability, prediction or aggregate performance: a description adequate for an institution's performance can merge states its members' claims must distinguish, so adequacy is fixed by the evaluative target, and the target cannot be justified solely by the description that preserves it | A21 §18's Candidate 2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, with A21 §5's clause against circularity and A22's Construction C ([CASE-110](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-110.md)). A21: "no coarse-graining may be treated as generally normatively adequate solely because it preserves organizational stability, predictive accuracy, or aggregate performance." The case is demonstrated: total output preserves an institution's every judgment and merges a member's claim. The general conclusion is interpretive. It is [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md)'s target-relativity carried from individuation to evaluation, and [CLAIM-060](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-060.md) in the language of coarse-graining. Filed in distributed-agency because its case is a whole against its members. The sharp edge: it does not say which target is right, and it denies that the description can settle it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md) v6 | An organization's access to a signal, the signal's authority over action, and action on it are separable, and adaptive regulation keeps the first while making the second conditional on evidence; overcontrol, which buys freedom from harmful acts by cutting access or making inhibition unconditional, is a maladaptive regime and not more control, so flexibility is a context-sensitive property of maintained influence relations, not of how much is inhibited | The owner's idea, U42 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A41's line that an organization "could become extremely resistant to internal changes while losing its capacity to learn, correct errors, or act at all": "useful connections to the ACT and DBT frameworks here, which provide us with accounts/ontologies of maladaption and productive flexibility". In A42's form: recognizing a signal, granting it authority and acting on it are three steps; ACT's defusion is a mechanism for [CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)'s decoupling; DBT adds bounded stabilization before correction; RO-DBT names overcontrol as maladaptive. The sharp edge: these are analogies from human treatment, the organizational classes are A42's proposals, not diagnoses, and RO-DBT's own evidence is "promising but not definitive". | Active |
| [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md) v2 | A coarse-graining preserves a deterministic judgment exactly when the judgment is constant on its fibres: the judgment then factors through the coarse description, uniquely on its image, and otherwise two states the judgment tells apart have been merged | A21 §3 and §18 (Candidate 1) of the exchange of 2026-10-17, and A22's Construction A: for a judgment J and a coarse-graining C on the same states, J = j∘C for some j exactly when C(x₁) = C(x₂) implies J(x₁) = J(x₂). Granted, because it is elementary (the universal property of a quotient) and Ak's; the proof is in the body. It is [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md)'s judgment-valued special case with the converse added: [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) says a partition sufficient for one target need not be for another, and this says which partitions serve a deterministic judgment, those whose fibres lie inside its level sets, so the coarsest is the judgment's own partition. The sharp edge: it says when a description keeps a judgment, never whether the judgment is right. A21's probabilistic and causal versions are recorded in the body, not claimed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-351](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) | A zero aggregate gradient does not show that the demands it aggregates are reconciled: with positive weights it holds both when every demand's own gradient vanishes and when nonzero gradients cancel, and in the second case no update improves them all to first order; even the first is only joint first-order stationarity, which a demand's maximum or saddle also has | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." With L₁ = (θ − 1)² and L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0 ([CASE-115](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-115.md)), the equal-weight gradient is zero and the aggregate is at its global minimum, while each loss is 1 and wants the opposite move. In general a vanishing positive combination of gradients is either every gradient zero or a certificate that no update improves them all, and the scalar cannot tell which. The sharp edge: it is a fact about a weighted sum, not about what a monitor reading it represents. A29's "the unity of the distress signal need not arise from the unity of the underlying causes" is the interpretive reading, kept apart in the body. | Active |
| [CLAIM-352](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-352.md) v4 | Sen's two aspects of freedom divide along the record's line between what an agent can viably reach and the organization that selects among it: viable reachability can stand for the opportunity aspect only through a map from trajectories to valued functionings, which control theory does not supply, and will-organization gives a causal account of part of the process aspect, not of its fairness or legitimacy | The owner's connection, U11 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, quoting A9 and A10 on viable reachability: "This feels reminiscent of ideas from moral philosophy, e.g. Amartya Sen capabilities account." Worked out by A11. Sen's opportunity aspect is what reachability can represent, once a map says which reachable trajectories are valued functionings. The sharp edge: reachable states are not capabilities, and an efficacious governance is not a fair or legitimate process. | Active |
| [CLAIM-356](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-356.md) v3 | An objective that originates outside a learning system can become a goal of the training organization, through its causal role in selecting, stabilizing and reproducing the learned structure it rewards; exogenous origin does not disqualify a goal, but it does not show that the network governs or endorses the objective, and what is selected is performance on the updating distribution, not generalization | The owner's, U35 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, against A34's guardrail that "Loss minimization does not automatically mean the model has its own goals": the externally assigned objective "can motivate identification and persistence of learned features", so the training process can be described as "having endogenous goals". A35 granted it: "Yes, in a qualified but important sense", and weakened the generalization half, since selection is for performance on "the encounters and feedback distribution actually used for updating". It objects in part to [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md): it grants that a modeller-fixed objective does not show self-constitution, and denies that exogenous origin bars a goal from becoming the training organization's own regulation. The sharp edge: the goal belongs to the training organization ([CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md)), not to the network, and nothing here says the network endorses or governs it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) v5 | The frustration residual and governance regret separate structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and identify none of them as thwarting: a positive residual says no admissible update meets every declared requirement, a positive regret only that the actual update's worst residual exceeds the best achievable, which can hold while every requirement is met, and actual violation needs regret above the negative residual; aggregate performance does not tell infeasibility from realized violation, and the multipliers that certify infeasibility need not be the weights governance assigns | A34 §4 and A35 §3.3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, restated at A39 §2C and A40 §3.4, from A33's "irreducible conflict" and "manufactured frustration". With m(d) the worst residual, Φ its minimum and Γ the actual update's excess over Φ ([CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md)): Φ > 0 is structural infeasibility; when Φ ≤ 0 the actual update violates a requirement exactly when Γ > −Φ. Positive governance regret establishes excess worst-case shortfall relative to the optimum, and can hold while every requirement is met. Neither quantity identifies an obstructing mechanism, a governance failure or active thwarting; governance-induced frustration needs an argument or intervention showing the allocation of influence responsible. A35: "Importantly, these dual multipliers are not endorsement weights." | Active |
| [CLAIM-359](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-359.md) v2 | A self-governing organization's robustness to compromised constituents is a property of the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, not only of its constraints on harmful acts; safeguards against capture can also restrict the disagreement and revision that self-governance needs, and where they do security and self-governance trade off, while others, such as audits independent of the audited that protect dissent, serve both, so the two are distinct achievements and not opposed ones | The owner's question, U41 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "is literature on organizational robustness to insider threats potentially useful to us?" A41's answer, condensed: an insider can aim at the organization's future allocation of authority rather than at the present decision, so robustness must protect the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, and the same protection can silence the opposition that corrects the organization, though some safeguards protect both. Insider threats and internal opposition can look alike. The sharp edge: Byzantine fault tolerance protects a fixed specification; this claim is about protecting the capacity to change it, which no protocol of that kind supplies. | Active |
| [CLAIM-360](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-360.md) v2 | The deep-versus-shallow learning results separate three effects that aggregate loss conflates: a larger realizable function class, a larger set reachable within a fixed data and compute budget, and a different internal organization with the same attainable outcomes; the deep linear results show the third, the random-hierarchy results the second, and the depth-separation result for products of inputs the first, at fixed size | The owner's, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's proposed experiment: "I think we may already have an empirical demonstration that would be useful here in the wide vs deep literature." A38 refined it into three effects, (A) enlarged realizable function class, (B) enlarged budgeted reachable set, (C) new internal organization without better attainable outcomes, filed Saxe et al. under C and the random hierarchy model under B, and said A "needs a separately established expressivity restriction". The record has one: Rolnick and Tegmark ([THEORY-206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-206.md)), a separation at fixed neuron count. The sharp edge: which effect a result shows depends on the budget, and A38 warned against "depth produces individuation while width merely provides redundant capacity". | Active |
| [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) v4 | A normative judgment is well-defined only once its relata are fixed (the organization or standpoint it concerns, the standard, the scale and the context), and that dependence does not by itself make it relative: once they are fixed, the judgment can be false | The owner's, U17 and U18 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "maybe part of what we've elucidated is that normative judgements necessarily rely on contexts and relations?", then "so maybe something like a frame/order/scale/perspectival-relative normative realism?" A17 put it as "Normative judgment is contextually constituted and relationally indexed, without necessarily being arbitrary or merely subjective", and A18 named the relata and split order into organizational and reflective order. The record held it only in pieces: [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) for individuation, [THEORY-220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-220.md) for function, [CLAIM-075](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md) for viability. Filed in will-organization, where the question of what organizes an agent's standards sits and where [CLAIM-075](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md) marks the limit, rather than pragmatic-transport, which holds the transport of judgments between contexts ([CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md), [QUESTION-130](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-130.md)) and not their indexing. The sharp edge: it is the constitutive half only. That the standards themselves can be objectively better or worse is not claimed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) v2 | On a norm-ball update set the local frustration residual Φ_r = min over ‖d‖ ≤ r of max_i(ε_i + g_iᵀd) equals the maximum over the simplex of Σλ_iε_i − r‖Σλ_ig_i‖_*, so infeasibility of the declared improvements has a certificate, and any admissible actual update exceeds Φ_r by a nonnegative governance regret | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The residual is the smallest worst-case shortfall of the declared local improvements ε_i over updates of size at most r. Minimax for the bilinear problem on two compact convex sets gives the dual over the simplex, so Φ_r > 0 exactly when some λ certifies that no update meets all demands (A34's form). Governance regret Γ is the gap between an actual admissible update's shortfall and Φ_r, and is never negative. For L₁ = (θ − 1)², L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0, Φ_r = ε for every r. The sharp edge: per A37 it is a cardinal refinement of the ordinal fact ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), and its magnitude depends on units (A36 §2D). | Active |
| [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) v3 | Whether several objectives share a strict first-order descent direction, 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, is invariant under smooth invertible reparameterization, while the sign of a Euclidean gradient inner product is not, and a negative inner product does not exclude common descent; a budgeted version is invariant only with the metric pulled back | A35 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, at the owner's U35 "double click" on whether functionally equivalent parameterizations give equivalent frustration diagnoses. Gradients transform as g′ = Jᵀg and directions as v′ = J⁻¹v, so directional derivatives, and with them the common-descent test 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, do not depend on coordinates. A Euclidean inner product does: g₁ = (1, 1), g₂ = (1, −½) have product ½, and under θ = diag(½, 2)ψ their transforms have −7/4, while d = (−1, 0) lowers both throughout. The sharp edge: it covers coordinate changes of one parameter space at first order, not function-preserving symmetries or training trajectories ([QUESTION-127](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-127.md)). The practice corollary, not to diagnose task conflict by gradient cosine, is the anthology's. | Active |
| [CLAIM-368](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md) v4 | The primitive for an organization's regulatory difficulty is frustration, not distress: a relation between maintained, consequential demands and the incompatibilities, constraints or countervailing processes that limit their realization, independent of strain, the burden of sustaining activity, and distinct from distress, a possible integrated response to either | The owner's, U33 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "maybe we should focus less on distress and more on frustration". A33 granted it: "Frustration is the most promising theoretical primitive of the three." Frustration is a fact about demands, admissible transformations and governance, so it can be stated without feelings and without a common scale. It supersedes in substance the distress-first formulations of A28–A32, which were never filed. The sharp edge: it says what to start from, not that a frustrated organization is distressed or feels anything. The claim bears on the organizational-affect line, which is Deferred ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md)); whether that line reopens is the owner's decision, not made here. | Active |
| [CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) | In symmetric resource-mediated competition with interaction matrix A = UᵀU and growth rates r = Uᵀb − c, Lotka–Volterra population dynamics are multiplicative gradient flow on the convex feature-selection objective ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn over the nonnegative orthant: the invasion fitness of an absent component is the negative partial derivative of that objective, and the uninvadable equilibria are its KKT points | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof. When competition between components is mediated by shared resources with feature or niche vectors u_i, so that A = UᵀU and r = Uᵀb − c, the Lotka–Volterra dynamics are ṅ_i = −n_i ∂_i L with L(n) = ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn: entropic mirror descent on the positive orthant. A rare component's invasion fitness is −∂_i L, the value of adding that feature, and uninvadable equilibria are the KKT points of the convex program. The sharp edge: the identity needs a shared scalar objective, and it fails for asymmetric interactions or processes with competing objectives, which is where an organization stops being an optimizer. Mehta et al. (2019) and Marsland, Cui and Mehta (2020) give the general duality for consumer–resource models. | Active |
| [CLAIM-370](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-370.md) | For a symmetric positive-pair distribution with marginal p, the conditional-expectation operator on L²(p) has the density ratio K⁺ as its kernel, and it is Hilbert–Schmidt exactly when the χ²-divergence of the pair from the product of its marginals is finite, in which case it is compact and self-adjoint with an orthonormal eigenbasis | [THEORY-005](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md)'s derivation, stated as the record's own and with its proof. Johnson et al. ([LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md)) write the operator on a finite space without an integrability condition. HaoChen et al. ([LIT-249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-249.md)) reach the Hilbert– Schmidt property from a uniform bound, which is stronger. Here the condition is exact: Hilbert–Schmidt if and only if finite χ². It says nothing about what trained features span. | Active |
| [CLAIM-371](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-371.md) | Under the componentwise order on distortion profiles, two profiles are incomparable exactly when they trade off, and then positive weightings can rank them either way, while every positive weighting agrees with a dominance | The order-theoretic part of [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md), on its own so that it can carry its own warrant. It says nothing about translation, what the components measure, or which weighting a task fixes. Only that, under the componentwise order of [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md), a trade-off is incomparability, that a trade-off can be resolved either way by positive weights, and that a dominance cannot. | Active |
| [CLAIM-372](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-372.md) | Within a fixed measurement scenario, the contextual fraction is a piecewise-linear and Lipschitz-continuous function of the empirical model's probability table, with a constant that depends only on the scenario | The record's own derivation, from the linear programme of Abramsky, Barbosa and Mansfield ([LIT-265](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md), Eq. 3), which [THEORY-165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md) holds. The non-contextual fraction is the minimum of the dual objective over finitely many vertices, so it is concave and piecewise linear in the probability table, and the contextual fraction is Lipschitz in it. The constant is the largest ℓ₁ norm of a dual vertex, which depends only on the scenario and is not bounded here. Nothing here crosses scenarios or applies to signalling data. | Active |
| [CLAIM-373](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-373.md) | If a map approximately intertwines two operators, with defects E_A = ΦA − A′Φ and E_B = ΦB − B′Φ, then Φ[A,B] − [A′,B′]Φ = A′E_B + E_A B − B′E_A − E_B A, so the commutator is carried to within (‖A‖ + ‖A′‖)‖E_B‖ + (‖B‖ + ‖B′‖)‖E_A‖ | The commutator-distortion identity of the manuscript's §9, on its own and proved. A map that nearly intertwines each of two operations carries their commutator to the commutator of the images, up to an error that is linear in the two intertwining defects. [ARG-006](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-006.md) is the exact case. It says nothing about whether the defects can be identified from data ([CLAIM-253](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md)), or what bounds an observed order effect ([CLAIM-231](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-231.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-374](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-374.md) | On a consistently connected system, Contextuality-by-Default and the sheaf criterion agree: a maximally connected coupling exists exactly when a global law has the contexts' laws as its marginals | The record's derivation of what [NOTE-600](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-600.md) marks as its own inference. In a consistently connected system, every observable has one distribution in all the contexts that contain it. Then each connection's maximal coupling makes its copies equal with probability 1 ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md), Theorem 3.3), so a maximally connected coupling is a joint law of one variable per observable, which is a global section in Abramsky and Brandenburger's sense ([LIT-016](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md), [THEORY-012](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md)). Conversely, a global section gives such a coupling. The two criteria come apart only when marginals shift with context. | Active |
| [CLAIM-375](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md) | Under one-hop allocation within an epoch, an operator that endorses an ally whose policy is nearer its own than the collective decision is raises how far its preferred policy is realized while its own authority stays fixed, so the two conditions of the endorsement scheme hold together | The demonstrated core of [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md). Under A3's one-hop rule I_j = I_j⁰ + Σ_(k≠j) b_k E_kj, with budgets and baselines fixed within an epoch ([CLAIM-282](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md)), an operator's authority does not respond to its own endorsements. If the collective decision is the authority-weighted mean of the operators' policies, then endorsing an ally whose policy is nearer one's own than the decision is moves the decision strictly toward one's policy. So the reward for realized policy, and not for held authority, pays for delegating. It does not say operators behave so, or that any rule beyond one hop keeps both conditions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-376](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-376.md) | A linear system that is stable at every instant can have a positive Lyapunov exponent: shifting any operator with exponent λ > 0 by −δI lowers its exponent by exactly δ and makes every instantaneous operator stable, so for 0 < δ < λ the shifted system is stable at every instant and unstable | The case [THEORY-724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md)'s source asserts and does not show. If A(t) has first Lyapunov exponent λ > 0, the propagator of A(t) − δI is e^(−δt)Φ(t), so its exponent is exactly λ − δ, while every eigenvalue of every A(t) moves left by δ. Applied to the undamped oscillator switching ω between 0.5 and 3 every unit of time: λ = 0.1955, and with δ = 0.1 the system is stable at every instant, with eigenvalues −0.1 ± 3i and −0.1 ± 0.5i, and has exponent 0.0955. | Active |
| [CLAIM-377](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-377.md) | For any differentiable model under squared loss with Gaussian noise of precision β, the model's Fisher on n inputs is the Gauss–Newton matrix βJᵀJ, and its non-zero eigenvalues are exactly β times those of the empirical NTK Gram matrix JJᵀ, with the same multiplicities, its eigenvectors being Jᵀ applied to the Gram matrix's, normalized | [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s Step 1, stated as the record's own and proved. Through the SVD J = UΣVᵀ, JᵀJ and JJᵀ share the non-zero eigenvalues σ_i² with equal multiplicities, and Jᵀu/σ is the eigenvector of JᵀJ for a unit eigenvector u of JJᵀ. Under y \| x ~ N(f(x; θ), β⁻¹), the expected outer product of the score is β∇f∇fᵀ, which summed over inputs is βJᵀJ, the Gauss–Newton matrix. "Fisher" means the model's Fisher, not the empirical Fisher of observed residuals. It holds at every width, in every regime and on any data. It says nothing about what the spectrum looks like, which is [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s. | Active |
| [CLAIM-378](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-378.md) | A representational similarity index invariant to every invertible linear map depends on a representation only through its column space, so it takes one value on all column-centred representations of rank n − 1, as it does on all representations of rank n | The generalization of [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md)'s theorem. If col(X) = col(Y), write X = BC and Y = BD with B a basis of the common column space and C, D of full row rank, extend C and D to invertible matrices, and the quotient maps X onto Y. Since XA always has the column space of X, the GL(p) orbits are exactly the sets of n × p matrices sharing a column space. Theorem 1 is the case of column space ℝⁿ. Column-centred matrices of rank n − 1 all have column space 1^⊥, so an invariant index cannot tell them apart either. | Active |
| [CLAIM-379](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-379.md) | On a finite set of stimuli, regularized linear readouts with ridge b > 0 cannot tell apart two centred representations of the same width exactly when one is an orthogonal transformation of the other, and the unregularized CCA member cannot tell apart representations with the same column space, which differ by an invertible linear map | The proved core of [CLAIM-269](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md). What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of K_X = X G⁻¹ Xᵀ/M, with G = aC_X + bI ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)). For b > 0, K_X and the Gram matrix XXᵀ determine each other, by a monotone map on the shared eigenvalues; and equal Gram matrices mean an orthogonal transformation ([CLAIM-290](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md), [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)). For b = 0, K_X is the projection onto the column space, which fixes X only up to an invertible linear map, as for a softmax layer ([THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-380](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-380.md) v2 | With finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, the positive part of the Bayes-risk increase on the same decision problem is directed, is zero from a garbling back to its source, vanishes for every finite problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source, and has A86's D_Q as its symmetrization | The finite-outcome part of [CLAIM-326](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-326.md). Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺, with losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior. A garbling never gains. The term is directed. A86's D_Q is its symmetrization. And with every finite problem and prior, it vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by Blackwell's Theorem 6 ([THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). It does not cover outcome spaces that are not finite, or say this is the right decision term. | Active |
| [CLAIM-381](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) | Over a finite class of items with finite judgement outcomes, a constant outcome kernel fits every item only when the target readers' averaged responses do not vary with the item, an exact fit is a garbling with the item as common parameter, and Le Cam's deficiency and its restriction to finitely many decision problems are finite computations | The derivational core of [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md). Over a finite class of items, the target term is the readers' response averaged over a procedure's output, and one outcome kernel family is fixed across the items. Then a constant kernel fits only target responses that carry no information about the item. An exact fit is a garbling, with the item as the common parameter. And Le Cam's deficiency between the two finite tables is one linear programme. Its restriction to finitely many decision problems is a finite computation. It does not say the measure is informative, which is [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md)'s empirical question. | Active |
| [CLAIM-382](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-382.md) | In an autoencoder initialised with i.i.d. Gaussian weights and zero biases and trained by SGD or momentum SGD on a loss of its output, the law of each hidden layer's learned representation is invariant under every orthogonal map of that layer that commutes with its activation, so under a radial activation no basis is privileged in law, while elementwise tanh or Leaky-ReLU yields invariance only under the signed permutations or the permutations, which leaves the standard axes free to be privileged | [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s symmetry argument, stated as the record's own and proved. Transform the parameters by orthogonal maps Q_l of the hidden spaces that commute with the activation. The network then computes Q_l h_l and the same output, so the loss is invariant. Gradient steps commute with the transformation, and an i.i.d. Gaussian initialisation is invariant under it, so the law of the trained representations is too. For radial activations this is all of O(n), and no basis is privileged in law. For elementwise ones it is a finite group, so the axes may be privileged. Whether they are, and how strongly, is [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s empirical content. | [CLAIM-383](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-383.md) | In plane Couette and plane Poiseuille flow, measured in the energy norm, the linearized operator about the laminar profile has transient growth at least cR and resolvent norm at least cR² with c independent of R, so wherever it is eigenvalue-stable a perturbation of norm at most CR⁻² makes it eigenvalue-unstable | [THEORY-304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md)'s scalings as lower bounds, derived. At streamwise wavenumber zero, the cross-stream velocities obey an R-independent Stokes problem in the time t/R. They force the streamwise velocity through −U′v, so the streamwise response is R times an R-independent field. In the energy norm this gives transient growth at least cR, and in the steady forced problem a resolvent norm at least cR². Through pseudospectra, a perturbation of norm O(R⁻²) then moves an eigenvalue into the unstable half-plane wherever the flow is eigenvalue-stable. The sharp constants, and that the growth is no more than order R, come from the computation and are not here. | Active |
| [CLAIM-384](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-384.md) | For a network linearised at its initial parameters, with an isotropic Gaussian prior of precision α on the parameter displacement and Gaussian noise of precision β, the log-determinant part of the evidence is −½ Σ log(1 + βλ/α) over the non-zero eigenvalues λ of the empirical neural tangent kernel's Gram matrix on the training inputs, so at most n directions are priced however many parameters the network has |  | Active |
| [CLAIM-385](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-385.md) v2 | If a symmetric operator on ℝⁿ commutes with an orthogonal representation of a compact group, each eigenspace is a sum of real irreducibles and each multiplicity a sum of multiples of their dimensions, so SO(2) and ℤ/n for n ≥ 3 force paired eigenvalues; conversely the spectrum fixes neither the group nor a basis inside an eigenspace |  | Active |
| [CLAIM-386](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-386.md) | For x(t+1) = (A* + εC)x with A* block-diagonal, the Simon–Ando aggregate Â = QAV has one-step closure defect exactly QA − ÂQ = QA(I − VQ); the part from the blocks' own dynamics vanishes iff every block has equal column sums, and then the whole defect is ε·QC(I − VQ) | Derived in the reading of Shpak, Stadler, Wagner and Altenberg (2004), [NOTE-977](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-977.md), which states the Simon–Ando aggregate without an error term, and re-checked here. | [CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md) | Optimal deterministic information-bottleneck partitions at two budgets need not be nested: with X uniform on four states and binary Y with P(Y=1\|x) = (0, 0, 1/8, 3/8), the optimum is {0,1,2 \| 3} for 6.91 < β < 9.26 and {0,1 \| 2,3} for 9.26 < β < 16.06, two partitions neither of which refines the other | Found by brute force in the reading of Equitz and Cover ([NOTE-988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-988.md)) and re-run here from scratch. It says nothing about stochastic encoders, where finite-β optima generally live ([THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-388](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md) v3 | Exact dynamical closure of a collective variable does not require a nearly decomposable block: in a linear Gaussian VAR(1) with uniform coupling among n units, the sum of all units is exactly dynamically independent at every stable coupling strength, while every partition of the units into two or more groups couples as strongly across its edges as within them | From A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, which gave the two-unit continuous-time case (ż = (b − a)z for z = x₁ + x₂) and the boxed slogan "Exact aggregation ⇏ near-decomposability". It does not say the closed sum is one system ([QUESTION-218](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-218.md)), and it is about partitions of the units: in the eigenbasis of A the same system is exactly decomposable, which is the point. | Active |
| [CLAIM-389](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-389.md) v2 | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), exact dynamical independence of a linear coarse-graining implies that its Mori–Zwanzig memory vanishes, but not conversely: memory needs coupling out of the coarse variable and back, and dependence needs only the way back, so a coarse variable can be Markov in its own law with zero memory and still be dynamically dependent | Derived in the reading of Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2000), [NOTE-989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-989.md), and re-checked here. | [CLAIM-390](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-390.md) | For a block of coordinates in a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), dynamical dependence is at most ½ log det(I + Σ_YY⁻¹ A_YR C A_YRᵀ), with A_YR the coupling into the block and C the covariance of the rest given the block's present state, so it is of second order in the coupling into the block, whatever the coupling out of it | First found in the reading of Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2000), [NOTE-989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-989.md), as a by-product; derived and checked here. | [CLAIM-391](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-391.md) | For any classes with weights π_c and per-class factor matrices H_c and Δ_c, the class-wise Kronecker product Σ_c π_c H_c ⊗ Δ_c exceeds the product of the weighted averages H̄ ⊗ Δ̄ by exactly the weighted between-class covariance Σ_c π_c (H_c − H̄) ⊗ (Δ_c − Δ̄), so the two agree when either factor is the same in every class |  | Active |
| [CLAIM-392](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-392.md) v2 | Stochastic information-bottleneck optima at two budgets need not be nested: for X uniform on four states and binary Y with P(Y=1\|x) = (0, 0, 1/8, 3/8), the unique optima at β = 8 and β = 12 admit no Markov chain X → T₂ → T₁, so raising the budget reorganizes the optimum even with noisy encoders | Computed in the reading of Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani (2023), [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md), on the source of [CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md), and re-run here. The certificate is numerical, not interval arithmetic, and the loss is small: 0.49% of the larger budget, in unique information. | Active |
| [CLAIM-394](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-394.md) | In a stationary linear Gaussian VAR(1) that is time-reversible (AΠ = ΠAᵀ, Π the stationary covariance), every slow-feature direction is a left eigenvector of A, so any span of slow features is an exactly dynamically independent coarse-graining; off reversibility a slow feature is in general neither independent nor free of memory | Derived in the reading of Schüler and Wiskott (2025), [NOTE-1015](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md), and re-checked here. It says when slowness, the criterion of slow feature analysis ([THEORY-746](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-746.md)), picks out a closed coarse-graining in [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md)'s sense: always in the reversible linear Gaussian VAR(1), which is the class of noise-free square mixtures of independent AR(1) processes, and not in general otherwise. | [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) | Under Montévil and Mossio's definition of closure, a closed set of constraints has at least two members, and if each constraint is produced at the time scale of a constraint in the set that generates it and not at the scale at which it is itself conserved, the set includes at least one slow and one fast dependence, so a system with a single constraint of its own cannot realise closure |  | Active |
| [CLAIM-397](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-397.md) v2 | For a scalar stationary process with autocovariance C, the Mori–Zwanzig memory kernels for the projection onto the current value are fixed by C alone, through C(m+1) = Σ_{k≤m} c_k C(m−k); the memory vanishes iff C is geometric, and when C has finite Hankel rank d the memory has Hankel rank exactly d − 1 | Derived in the reading of Lin and Lu (2019), [NOTE-1029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1029.md), and re-checked here. | [CLAIM-398](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-398.md) | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1) on ℝⁿ, a scalar linear coarse variable Y = LX is, in its own law, an ARMA process of orders at most (n, n − 1); so its Mori–Zwanzig memory, though non-zero at every lag in general, is carried exactly by finitely many coordinates that are functions of Y's own past and innovations | Derived in the reading of Chorin and Lu (2015), [NOTE-1028](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1028.md), and re-checked here. Their NARMAX closures are fitted, with no error bound; in the linear Gaussian class the same idea is exact. | [CLAIM-399](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-399.md) | Causal abstraction in the senses of Rubenstein et al., Beckers and Halpern, and Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern does not secure governance-response sufficiency: exact transformation, τ-abstraction and zero approximate-abstraction distance all accept the hidden-bit coarse-graining, which loses ρ(h = 1) bits of the response to h, because each lets high-level noise carry what the coarse state drops; for one outcome and the identity correspondence, sufficiency is their compatibility condition with the high-level context fixed to the coarse state, and strong abstraction rejects the case only through interventions on the hidden parameter | The record's join, on 2026-10-21, of its readings of the causal-abstraction papers ([NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md), [NOTE-1032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1032.md), [NOTE-1045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1045.md)) with [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md). | [CLAIM-400](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-400.md) v3 | In the meaning–authority model linearized at symmetry, a third, maintained legibility state that authority moves (ε) and that moves interpretation (ν) or endorsement (μ), with persistence λ < 1 and nonnegative couplings, destabilizes the symmetric state exactly when the two-variable condition holds with β + νε/(1 − λ) in place of β and δ + με/(1 − λ) in place of δ: at the threshold the regime is indistinguishable from stronger two-variable couplings, and the slower it is the more it adds, while away from the threshold it adds a mode that no two-variable model has, so a lean in the regime can outlast the advantages it was built from | [QUESTION-253](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-253.md) asked whether authority's effect on what becomes legible as evidence is a third channel with its own instability condition, or [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md)'s κ′ renamed. Both, in different respects. With a maintained legibility state r, det(I − J₃) = (1 − λ)[(1 − α)(1 − δ) − βγ] − ε[νγ + μ(1 − α)], which is (1 − λ) times [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)'s expression with β_eff = β + νε/(1 − λ) and δ_eff = δ + με/(1 − λ). | [CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) v3 | The conditions an effective description is commonly asked to meet are not of one kind: predictive sufficiency and approximation fidelity are adequacy relative to a declared target, metric and horizon; tractability restricts the operations under which adequacy is assessed; dynamical independence and memory closure are relations of the representation to the system, memory relative to a chosen projection; so a matrix over them as independent binary axes conflates kinds | A4 and A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U4 ("it sounds like considering it from this angle has potentially already altered our characterization of those 'virtues'"). | [CLAIM-403](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md) v5 | A contribution's admission to an organization's inquiry, its recognition in apt terms, its credibility, its uptake into judgements, and its contributor's part in revising the standards of uptake are separable, each possible without the later ones, so an organization can widen access while every channel by which a less authoritative contribution could change the criteria of authority stays closed | A24 §6 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U24: "Someone's contribution may be received and politely acknowledged yet have no mechanism through which it can change institutional understanding." | [CLAIM-421](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md) v4 | The cessation of an organizational perspective's enactment need not imply the loss of the dispositions, capacities or reproductive relationships from which it can be reinstated: an interruption can be of activation (the disposition is held but not engaged or retrievable), of enactment (held, but the material, institutional or social conditions for exercising it are gone) or of reproduction (held by some bearers, but the processes that pass it on are damaged), and temporary unavailability is not extinction, though prolonged interruption of reproduction can end a tradition | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22, at the owner's U37: the doorway effect as perspective meeting grounded experience, and the perspectival interruptions of the Chinese Cultural Revolution. | [CLAIM-434](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-434.md) | On a finite set of outcomes, some function rises with every move that wins one of a negotiation's conflicts exactly when no chain of winning moves returns to where it began, and the length of the longest such chain ending at an outcome is one such function; a perfectly transitive record of which side won each pair, in a complete tournament contesting every pair once, leaves a cyclic share of (n − 2)/3n under the Hodge decomposition, a baseline that does not carry to sparse records; the Hodge gradient can reverse a comparison the wins settle, netting a record erases alternation, a record fixes a class of potentials rather than one, a coherent record is not yet one aligned with any single perspective's ordering, a best-fitting ordering of a cycle is no Lyapunov function, the sign a class of potentials gives can be set-valued, and an ordering fitted to a record overstates its agreement there | The formal core of the rename of 2026-10-23 from "ascendancy" to "potential" ([TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md)). | [CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md) v3 | An instantaneous ordering is a common currency on a finite set of options, where every complete preorder has a real-valued representation, but not in general: the lexicographic order on the unit square has no real-valued representation, while a continuous complete preorder on a connected separable space has a continuous one; so admitting an ordering is strictly weaker than admitting a currency, a graded lexicographic override lies in the gap while an exact threshold override does not, a threshold override with a discrimination threshold is a lexicographic semiorder whose choices can cycle and so is no ordering at all, and even where each instant has a currency, successive currencies need not share exchange rates | The formal half of the owner's reframing of 2026-10-23, that a "common currency" is better read as a negotiation admitting an (at least instantaneous) ordering. | [CLAIM-452](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-452.md) | For an organization whose response in each probe context is the authority-weighted mixture of its processes' known response profiles, the authority shares are identifiable from a set of contexts exactly when the processes' stacked profiles over those contexts are affinely independent; because the response is linear in the shares, local and global identifiability coincide, the condition is that the Fisher information of any design supported on those contexts is positive definite on the simplex's tangent space, and with binary outcomes at least one context fewer than there are processes is needed | When an organization's response in context c is p_π(·\|c) = Σᵢ πᵢ pᵢ(·\|c), the mixture [CLAIM-444](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-444.md) reduces the replicator model to, which probe contexts reveal its authority shares π? Exactly those over which the profiles are affinely independent. The response is linear in π, so there is no gap between local and global identifiability, and the condition is the Fisher information of [CASE-159](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-159.md)'s pullback being positive definite on the tangent space of the simplex. Each binary context adds at most one rank, so k processes need at least k − 1 contexts. It is a condition checkable before any data, which is what [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) asks for; none of the three works read on 2026-10-25 states it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-453](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-453.md) v2 | A population of perspectives, each advocating one of two interpretations, makes its collective choice by drift diffusion when the coordinate the decision is read from integrates independent evidence with no net leak or self-reinforcement and commitment is a bound on that coordinate; two interpretations make the reduction one-dimensional, but they do not by themselves give it | The owner's hypothesis at U34 of the exchange of 2026-10-24, continued: "if we've set up our simulation appropriately, when n=2 we should see drift diffusion dynamics". | [CLAIM-455](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-455.md) | For one bounded observer, a transformation of a representation can make one task's distinction legible and another's illegible at once, so legibility regimes are ordered only relative to a task, and a regime that improves one perspective's competence can disable another's | Stated in [CASE-154](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-154.md)'s title and its "What it can show" and held by no claim, found in the audit of 2026-10-27 for propositions cases state that no claim holds. The edge: one observer, two tasks; nothing about which task matters. | Active |
| [CLAIM-457](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-457.md) | That no single institution can bring about a remedy does not imply that no combination of them can: the institutions able together to realize a corrective outcome need include none able alone, so a true statement of unilateral inability is not a statement that the outcome is unattainable | A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-26, on the owner's CECOT case at U7: the United States said it could not bring a man back from Salvadoran custody, and El Salvador's president that he could not send him. | [CLAIM-458](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-458.md) v2 | A reception split between populations with unequal access to the source can be partly a difference of access and not of weighting, so a comparison of their default tasks can fit weights only on the components every population compared can perceive | The limit [CLAIM-240](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-240.md)'s note of 2026-10-10 recorded and did not code, filed as an objection. | [CLAIM-459](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-459.md) | An input to a bistable balance of authority can be sincere and causally efficacious without changing which regime operates: below a threshold the structure of the competition sets, it moves the balance within the current basin, so a higher-order volition that changes nothing visible need not be idle | Stated in [CASE-112](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-112.md)'s title and its first "What it can show" bullet and held by no claim, found in the audit of 2026-10-27. In ẇ = μw − w³ + h with μ > 0, the operative regime changes only when \|h\| passes 2μ^{3/2}/(3√3); for 0 < h < h_c the input moves w and leaves the regime. A8 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "An endorsement can be sincere and causally efficacious while remaining too weak to shift the system out of its current attractor basin." The edge: efficacy on the balance, not on behaviour; the claim says a null in behaviour is no evidence of a null input. | Active |
| [CLAIM-462](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md) v3 | An arrangement of institutions can keep, or increase, its capacity for effective action while its capacity to be effectively corrected by others degrades, because the two are maintained by different relations, so the first is no evidence of the second | A8's candidate central result and A9's conjecture, from the exchange of 2026-10-26: "A complex institutional system can preserve or even increase its capacity for effective action while losing its capacity for effective correction." It carries [CLAIM-422](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-422.md) (a correction is not a maintained capacity to correct) and [CLAIM-099](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-099.md) (effective action is not governance among regimes) from one organization to correction by other institutions. | [CLAIM-463](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-463.md) | Restoring the conditions under which a capacity was lost need not restore the capacity: where the activity that maintains it reinforces itself, the same conditions can sustain both the capacity and its absence, so a capacity lost past a threshold returns only under conditions better than those it was lost under, or by rebuilding the activity directly, and restoring it can cost more than preserving it would have | A4's claim candidate from the exchange "About the Chagossians" of 2026-10-26, "Resource restoration does not imply organizational restoration", which the first filing declined because [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md) already derives it; the owner asked for it to be filed as a claim with its connection to the case. | [CLAIM-464](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md) v2 | An intervention can change what it would take to correct it: by altering the distribution of control, access, resources or enforcement before it is reviewed, it can make a specified corrective outcome costlier or unreachable while the standards that govern that outcome stay the same | A7 to A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-26, from the owner's U6 and U7: the police entry at USIP before any court ruled, the East Wing demolished before review, and transfers into foreign custody. | [CLAIM-469](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-469.md) v2 | Luria is an apparatus for a record's objects in the operational sense: through its schemes, vocabularies, validators and generated views it realizes a system of distinctions that fixes what counts as a referable and governable object within the record, so that a split scheme makes one object two and a promoted vocabulary makes a value an entity; it keeps, enforces and propagates those distinctions; and its distinctions are revised through the record's own use | The operational half of [CLAIM-476](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md), split from it at the owner's review of the pull request. In [TERM-089](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-089.md)'s sense, which needs no observer and no constitutive metaphysics, luria differentiates, retains, enforces and revises distinctions among a record's entries. That is established by how its grammar works ([CLAIM-479](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-479.md)) and by the record's own amendments ([CLAIM-419](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md), [CASE-131](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-131.md), [CASE-178](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-178.md)). The further thesis that the record's objects are constituted in Barad's sense stays in [CLAIM-476](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md), which now rests on this one. Split so that luria's evidential role does not depend on accepting Barad's ontology. | Active |
| [CLAIM-470](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-470.md) v2 | Inquiry is a form of specification: a question fixes which differences would count as an answer, an inquiry adds the operations that make those differences accessible, and what it finds can stabilize into a specification that constrains later inquiry; so inquiry stands to its findings as a specification to its realizations, with one difference, that an inquiry can revise what an answer could be | The owner's, U15 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "inquiry is a form of specification." It carries [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md)'s analogy into inquiry: question and finding stand as specification and realization, and a stabilized finding becomes a specification for the next inquiry. A15 and A16 found Dewey and Collingwood the nearest predecessors, and counterexample-guided abstraction refinement the nearest formal case. [TERM-065](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-065.md) already keeps a description apart from the regime it is judged under; the claim adds that the regime is itself a product of inquiry and can be its object. It does not say that inquiry makes what it investigates. | Active |
| [CLAIM-475](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md) v2 | Specifying is itself a resource-bounded realization: formulating a question takes time, concepts and computation as realizing a configuration takes energy and matter, so the questions an agent can ask are a product of what it has already realized; a stabilized specification is past inquiry stored so that later questions become cheaper to ask, and it can make other questions harder | The owner's, U17 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "resource constraints impact specification in exactly the same way as they impact realization. I can't interrogate a question that takes me more time than I have to even ask it." It extends [CLAIM-470](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-470.md): if inquiry is specification, specifying is a process with costs, and the feasible questions are bounded before any answering starts. A17 and A18 drew a consequence the record can use: [TERM-065](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-065.md) takes its query family as supplied, and this claim says that family is the output of bounded activity. A stable specification amortizes the work that made it, which is a separation of time scales ([CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)), and entrenches what it makes cheap. | Active |
| [CLAIM-479](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-479.md) | In the record a typed relation is more constrained than either of its relata: a claim's content is open prose, while `rests_on` fixes the scheme at both ends, has `supports` written as its converse and says what retiring its target leaves, and none of that moves when either claim's content does; so a relation's rigidity is a fact about the grammar, not evidence that the dependency it records is sound | The owner's, U6 of the exchange of 2026-10-27, against A5's "its relationships are explicitly represented rather than metaphysically primitive": "and yet interestingly, relations like "supports" are less flexible than the raw contents of either relata." Shown from luria.yaml, which A6 §6 read correctly. The relation's type is determinate where the relata's content is not, and that determinacy is no warrant for the dependency: [CLAIM-293](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md) is the demonstrated case. [CASE-131](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-131.md) is the instance in which the rigidity of a relation outran what its relata meant and the grammar was amended. | Active |
| [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md) v2 | Composing interactions can turn an interior into a constraint, and sometimes into a constraint of a new kind: in the chain E = ½k₁(x₁ − x₂)² + ½k₂(x₂ − x₃)², with x₂ internal and equilibrated, the boundary sees E_eff = ½·k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂)·(x₁ − x₃)², a coupling between x₁ and x₃ that neither part has; if the interior relaxes slowly, eliminating it leaves a history-dependent constraint, a memory kernel, so interconnection fixes an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories and separation of time scales decides only whether that constraint is approximately memoryless; and for cellular sheaves the reduced constraint can relate three boundary values where every relation among the parts is pairwise | From A22 §4 and A23 §IV of the exchange of 2026-10-27, which called composition "the most important missing mechanism" after the owner's U20. Eliminating an equilibrated interior leaves an effective boundary relation that no part has; an outside system interacting only with the boundary meets it as a constraint, and "The interior has effectively become apparatus." Baez and Fong's black-boxing functor is the general theorem for passive linear networks. The memory case ties it to Mori–Zwanzig and to [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md): interconnection yields an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories in every case, and separation of time scales decides only whether it is approximately memoryless. For cellular sheaves the reduction can need a richer relational vocabulary than the parts used (THEORY-1090; QUESTION-283). It is independent evidence for [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md), that constraints are realized by organization. | Active |
| [CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md) | Coupling does not by itself separate time scales: two identical undamped oscillators coupled with stiffness k have normal modes at ω₀ and √(ω₀² + 2k), nearly equal when k ≪ ω₀², and neither decays; separation comes where the coupling dissipates relative differences faster than collective ones, as in ẋ = −ax − k(x − y), ẏ = −ay − k(y − x), whose collective and relative modes relax at rates a and a + 2k, and in a Laplacian flow ẋ = −κLx, where the spectrum of L sets the rates | The answer A20, A21 and A23 gave to the owner's conjecture at U20 that coupling necessarily induces scale separation ([CLAIM-473](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-473.md)). Two small computations: conservative coupling splits modes without separating or damping them, and dissipative coupling damps the relative mode at a rate that grows with the coupling. For a Laplacian flow the kernel is exact compatibility and the nonzero spectrum is the hierarchy of relaxation rates, so a spectral gap is where the separation comes from. Conceded, so Active. It gives a mechanism for [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s second half and is not a test of individuality. | Active |
| [CLAIM-482](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-482.md) v2 | An organization's aggregate revealed preference exists exactly when its record of winning moves never cycles, and where it exists it is fitted to one regime of authority, so an intervention on authority that changes the winning moves changes the fitted preference and the preference does not predict the change | The status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) found the record's later formal work bearing on an objection it never cited. [CLAIM-089](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-089.md)'s aggregate version says Northstar "simply prefers speed": the governing relations are the organization's revealed preference. [CLAIM-434](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-434.md), Active and demonstrated, says when such a preference exists: an ordering that every winning move climbs exists exactly when the wins never cycle. So the objection is not refuted in general. It is true of an organization whose record is acyclic, and unavailable for one whose record cycles. Where it holds, the ordering is read off the wins under one regime of authority. [CASE-003](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-003.md) changes authority and holds attitudes and evidence fixed, and the wins change. Then the fitted ordering changes too, and nothing in the first ordering predicted the second. The revealed preference redescribes the outcome of the governing relations, which is the reading [CLAIM-027](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md)'s defeater excludes ("whose content predicts the outcome"). | Active |
| [CLAIM-485](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-485.md) v2 | In the self-governing sense, what endogenous governance adds over a behaviourally equivalent system with an external scheduler is not that it allocates authority among its own processes but that it can revise its own governing standards when they break down | The bridge the owner asked for on 2026-10-28, between Kahl's proposal (THEORY-1165), which is about agency in the sense that bears on responsibility, and [QUESTION-092](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-092.md), which fixes [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s sense 5, self-governing. It is the record's answer to the question. Internal allocation of authority, the second of [CLAIM-025](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md)'s separable capacities (governing among regimes), coordinates execution and does not make a system govern itself more than an external scheduler would. The capacity to revise its governing standards when they break down does: the third capacity, which [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) names as taking part in governing the conditions of its own transformation. Two systems matched within a regime differ under it, and they diverge in behaviour once that regime breaks down. | Active |
| [CLAIM-492](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-492.md) v2 | If the self is defined to include whatever an agent cares about, the claim that all motivation serves the self is true by definition and rules nothing out; the thesis has content only with a criterion of the self's extent that can come apart from what the agent cares about | The classic objection to psychological egoism (Butler; Sober and Wilson, [LIT-1683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1683.md)), turned on the owner's thesis. "Every motive is my motive" is trivially true and does not make every motive self-interested. "My self includes whatever I care about" makes the thesis unfalsifiable. It is answered if the thesis names an independent criterion of the self's extent, such as overlap, fusion or salient self-categorization, and predicts that motivation follows that criterion and not caring alone. | Active |
| [CLAIM-495](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-495.md) | For an O(d)-valued connection on a connected graph, the assignments that meet every edge relation xᵢ = Tᵢⱼxⱼ form a space isomorphic to the vectors at one vertex fixed by every holonomy based there, which is the kernel of the connection Laplacian; for d = 1, and for U(1) phases, that space is all or nothing, but for d > 1 a connection whose loops are not trivial can still keep a subspace on which every loop is, so compatibility among local frames can be partial and graded by direction; and edge maps that do not commute can compose to a flat loop, so non-commutativity is not holonomy | From A2 and A3 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), which drew it out of [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s O(d) setting against [THEORY-1082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1082.md)'s U(1) one. The proof and the example are the record's, checked numerically. It is the zeroth cohomology of the connection sheaf, so standard, and it says nothing about which organizations have such transports. | Active |
| [CLAIM-496](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md) | Agreement between routes of translation is a measure of coherence, not of fidelity, and the two are independent: a rendering that sends every source utterance to one output makes direct and relay transport agree exactly while a receiver who could tell a promise from a prediction with no error is left at chance, and two routes that keep the act and differ in register disagree completely while losing nothing the act-identification task needs | From A4 and A5 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), where the assistant carried [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s comparison of alternative paths over to translation and then warned that "path agreement is a coherence criterion, not a fidelity criterion". The constructions are the record's. It does not say path discrepancy is uninformative: it says it measures something [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md)'s directed loss does not, and conversely. | Active |
